records.summary: A mailing-list error sent letters containing customer details, including phone numbers, to incorrect recipients; Telstra said about 220,000 customers were affected. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Telstra suffered a mailing list error that resulted in approximately 60,300 letters being sent to incorrect addresses, exposing customer names, telephone plans and phone numbers to unauthorised recipients. The breach was particularly serious as it included 15,400 customers with silent lines (unlisted numbers) who had specifically paid for privacy protections.
records.sourceLabel: ABC News; Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: A series of denial-of-service attacks disrupted access to several federal government websites during the Operation Titstorm protest. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: In February 2010, the hacktivist group Anonymous launched Operation Titstorm, a series of distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks against Australian government websites in protest of proposed internet censorship regulations. The attacks rendered the Australian Parliament House website inaccessible for three days and disrupted access to multiple government services, accompanied by email spam, junk faxes, and prank phone calls to government offices.
records.sourceLabel: ABC News; Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: Vodafone said a shared password allowed an employee or dealer to access its customer database, exposing personal details; the company said millions of records could be accessible. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Vodafone Hutchison Australia's customer database was compromised through unauthorised access by employees and third-party dealers. Criminal groups obtained customer information including names, addresses and credit card details, while others used the access to monitor communications of partners and acquaintances.
records.sourceLabel: ABC News; Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: A cyber attack against the Australian domain registrar and hosting provider damaged customer-hosted websites and disrupted services. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Distribute.IT, an Australian domain registrar and web hosting provider, suffered a sophisticated cyber attack that permanently destroyed approximately 4,000 customer websites and email systems. The attackers not only wiped the servers but also destroyed all backup data, making recovery impossible and ultimately forcing the company out of business.
records.sourceLabel: The Register; Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The online retailer later disclosed a 2011 database breach involving customer account information and password data. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Catch of the Day, a popular Australian online retailer, suffered a database breach on 7 May 2011 that exposed hashed passwords and customer information including names, addresses, email details and some credit card numbers. The breach became controversial when the company waited nearly three years to notify affected customers.

AAPT reported a cyber incident involving customer information; contemporary records attributed the data exposure to a hacktivist intrusion. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: AAPT, an Australian telecommunications provider, had customer data stolen by the Anonymous hacktivist collective between 17 and 19 July 2012. The attackers accessed a database containing 264,691 customer names, 1,394 driver licence numbers and 13 sets of credit card details through vulnerabilities in outdated software on a server managed by Melbourne IT.
records.sourceLabel: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner; Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: Attackers exploited a server vulnerability and stole user records from the Australian online dating company; the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner investigated the incident.
records.sourceLabel: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner

records.organisation: Department of Immigration and Border Protection
records.summary: The department accidentally published a detention report containing embedded personal information about people held in immigration detention. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: The Department of Immigration and Border Protection (now Department of Home Affairs) accidentally published a detention report on its website containing the personal information of all 9,258 people in immigration detention. The report was publicly accessible for approximately eight and a half days before being removed, exposing highly sensitive information about asylum seekers including names, nationalities, detention locations and boat arrival details.
records.sourceLabel: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner; Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: An attacker stole customer databases from the travel insurer; reporting described hundreds of thousands of exposed records, with totals varying between sources. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Aussie Travel Cover, a travel insurance provider, suffered a data breach when a teenage hacker stole two databases containing over 870,000 customer records. The company was notified on 18 December 2014 but controversially chose not to inform affected policyholders, notifying only the third-party agents who sold the policies.
records.sourceLabel: ABC News; Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: Malware was found on Bureau of Meteorology systems after an intrusion; an Australian Cyber Security Centre report said documents were searched and likely copied.

Kmart disclosed unauthorised access to customer information associated with online orders. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Kmart Australia's online shopping platform was compromised by attackers who accessed customer names, email addresses, delivery and billing addresses, phone numbers and product purchase details. No credit card or payment information was stolen as Kmart uses a third-party payment gateway that does not store financial details internally.
records.sourceLabel: SBS News; Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The retailer said attackers accessed customer information held by its online shopping system. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: David Jones' online shopping website was hacked, with attackers accessing customer names, email addresses, order details and mailing addresses. The breach occurred just days after Kmart Australia revealed a similar incident, both affecting major Australian retailers in October 2015.
records.sourceLabel: ABC News; Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: Distributed denial-of-service attempts disrupted the online Census form and prompted the ABS to take the service offline; the agency said submitted data remained secure. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: On 9 August 2016, the Australian Bureau of Statistics eCensus system experienced four distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks that rendered the national Census website inaccessible for nearly two days. The attacks, which peaked at 7:28pm, overwhelmed the system due to IBM's failure to properly implement geoblocking protection. While no data was breached, the incident sparked the #CensusFail social media outcry and resulted in IBM paying a $30 million settlement for failing to meet its contractual obligations.
records.sourceLabel: Australian Bureau of Statistics; Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: A publicly accessible database file held by a website contractor was accessed, exposing personal and sensitive information relating to about 550,000 prospective blood donors. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: On 28 October 2016, the Australian Red Cross Blood Service disclosed that a database file containing personal and health information of approximately 550,000 prospective blood donors had been publicly accessible on a web server since 5 September 2016. A third-party contractor, Precedent Communications, had inadvertently placed the unencrypted file on a public-facing server. The breach was discovered by security researcher Troy Hunt and reported via AusCERT, prompting an immediate OAIC investigation into what was described as Australia's largest security breach at that time.
records.sourceLabel: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner; Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: Uber disclosed that attackers had accessed data belonging to 57 million drivers and riders worldwide in a 2016 breach, including users in Australia. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: In October-November 2016, attackers discovered AWS credentials in Uber's public GitHub repository and used them to access unencrypted backup files stored on Amazon S3, compromising data on 1.2 million Australian riders and 57 million users globally. Uber concealed the breach for over a year, paying the attackers US$100,000 through its bug bounty program to delete the data and remain silent. The breach was not disclosed until November 2017, following the appointment of a new CEO.
The recruitment and HR software provider detected unusual activity in its infrastructure; personal information held for Australian client organizations may have been compromised.
An intruder accessed ANU administrative systems and stole some personal information from records spanning 19 years; investigators could not determine the full extent of the data taken.

A sophisticated actor gained access to the Parliament House computer network; Australian authorities also investigated network activity affecting major political parties. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: The Australian Parliament House network was breached by what security agencies assessed to be a state-sponsored actor in early February 2019. The attack compromised the computer systems of major political parties including the Liberal, Labor, and National parties, accessing email accounts and parliamentary systems. This represents one of the most serious cyber attacks on Australian democratic institutions.
records.sourceLabel: ABC News; Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: Canva disclosed a cyber incident affecting user accounts worldwide; the Australian-headquartered company's investigation identified approximately 139 million affected accounts. The incident register reports: A profound infrastructure breach occurred when threat actor Gnosticplayers" bypassed production database perimeters. The threat actor stole user profiles containing real names; usernames; email addresses; and salted/hashed passwords for millions of global users." Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Canva, the Sydney-based graphic design platform, suffered a major data breach on 24 May 2019 affecting approximately 139 million user accounts globally. While Canva is a global platform, the breach of this major Australian technology company represented one of the largest data breaches involving an Australian-headquartered organisation. User information including email addresses, names, usernames, cities of residence, and hashed passwords was compromised.
records.sourceLabel: Australian Data Breach Archive; Supplied incident register (unverified)

records.summary: Cyber incident disrupted access to business systems and affected logistics operations.
Compromised staff email accounts exposed customer documents.
A legal services firm was hit by ransomware and threatened with publication of data stolen in the attack; the firm was not named in the report.
A cyber incident disrupted parts of the broadcaster's production and publishing operations.
A cyber incident disrupted clinical and administrative systems across the health and care network.
A global ransomware incident affected operations at the Australian meat producer.
A cyber attack on the payroll provider exposed personal information relating to nearly 80,000 South Australian government employees.

Personal information was accessed in a major telecommunications data breach. The incident register reports: Australia's second-largest telecommunications provider suffered a catastrophic security failure when an unauthenticated; internet-facing testing API was discovered by extortionists. The actor systematically exfiltrated full names; dates of birth; telephone numbers; physical addresses; email contacts; and millions of driver's licence and passport records [ID Number Redacted]. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Optus, Australia's second-largest telecommunications provider, suffered a data breach after an API endpoint was left publicly accessible without authentication. The breach exposed the personal information of nearly 10 million current and former customers.
records.sourceLabel: Incident overview; Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: A cyber incident resulted in the theft and publication of customer information. The incident register reports: Threat actors used stolen high-level credentials from a third-party IT service provider to gain access to Medibank's corporate network. The attackers exfiltrated highly sensitive customer data; including full names; dates of birth; Medicare numbers; and private medical diagnosis codes; before posting the data to a dark web leak site. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Medibank detected unusual activity on its network which was later confirmed to be a major ransomware incident. The attacker gained access using a stolen credential of a third-party contractor. When Medibank refused to pay the $15M ransom, the attackers published the data on the dark web.
records.sourceLabel: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner; Actor claim: blogxx; Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: MyDeal reported that a compromised credential was used to access its customer relationship system; approximately 2.2 million customers were affected. The incident register reports: Confirmed 5 Oct 2022. Woolworths subsidiary MyDeal suffered an administrative database exploit via a compromised user credential. Threat actors successfully exfiltrated a consumer repository containing 2.2 million customer profile logs; including names; DOBs; and addresses. Supermarket mainframes remained isolated. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

A cyber incident affected customer and applicant information held by the financial services provider. The incident register reports: Confirmed 16 Mar 2023. Massive consumer finance data disaster. 14;000;000 corporate records exfiltrated across Australia and New Zealand. The dataset included 7.9M driver's licences; 53;000 passport records; and 6.1M historical financial application logs dating back to 2005. Latitude refused all extortion demands. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Latitude Financial, a major Australian and New Zealand financial services company, suffered a data breach in March 2023 that ultimately affected 14 million customers and loan applicants. Attackers used a stolen employee login to access two service providers holding Latitude customer data, exposing 7.9 million driver's licence numbers and 53,000 passport numbers. The breach represents the largest theft of identity documents in Australian history.
records.sourceLabel: Latitude incident updates; Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: A cyber incident led to the theft and subsequent publication of law-firm data.

Pizza Hut said an unauthorised party accessed customer records affecting 193,000 people, including contact and delivery details. The incident register reports: Fast-food pizza franchise giant Pizza Hut Australia confirmed a localized e-commerce database breach. Threat actors exploited a web application vulnerability to harvest consumer order transaction tables; delivery details; and customer passwords. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Pizza Hut Australia confirmed a data breach in September 2023 affecting 193,000 customers after the threat actor ShinyHunters claimed to have stolen data from 1 million customers. The breach occurred between July and August 2023 when unauthorised actors gained access via an unprotected Amazon Web Services (AWS) endpoint. Exposed data included customer names, delivery addresses, email addresses, phone numbers, masked credit card numbers, and encrypted account passwords.
records.sourceLabel: ABC News; Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: A cyber security incident disrupted port operations across the Australian network. The incident register reports: Major maritime logistics operator DP World Australia abruptly suspended landside operations across container terminals in Sydney; Melbourne; Brisbane; and Fremantle following a critical network intrusion leveraging the CitrixBleed vulnerability. The incident crippled roughly 40% of the nation's incoming and outgoing maritime freight; stranding 30;000 containers. While internet systems were intentionally disconnected to isolate the breach and corporate network data exfiltration was confirmed; operational port management software was successfully insulated from ransom encryption. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: DP World Australia, a major port operator managing approximately 40% of goods entering and leaving Australia, detected unauthorised activity on its network on 10 November 2023. The company disconnected its network from the internet to contain the incident, forcing the closure of terminals in Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, and Fremantle for approximately one week. Whilst customer data was not affected, some employee personal information was accessed.
records.sourceLabel: DP World Australia; Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The Australian Government reported that personal and health information relating to prescriptions may have been exposed. The incident register reports: National e-prescription provider MediSecure suffered a catastrophic data breach compromising 12.9 million individual records; marking one of Australia's largest health sector exposures. Approximately 6.5TB of data—containing personal identities and sensitive prescription history up to November 2023—was exfiltrated from a server managed by a third-party vendor. The severe financial and operational fallout subsequently forced the company into voluntary administration. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: MediSecure, an electronic prescription delivery service provider, experienced a ransomware attack affecting approximately 12.9 million Australians—nearly half of the country's population. The breach exposed sensitive personal and health information including prescription details, Medicare numbers, and passport numbers, making it Australia's largest healthcare data breach.
records.sourceLabel: Australian Government; Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: Ticketek said customer names, email addresses and dates of birth were affected in a cyber security incident. The incident register reports: Confirmed 28 May 2024. Major Australian entertainment ticketing powerhouse Ticketek suffered a significant data breach originating from a compromised external cloud-hosted database platform. Customer registration profiles were exposed; OAIC formally updated. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Ticketek became aware on May 31, 2024 of a cyber incident affecting Ticketek Australia account holder information stored in a cloud-based platform hosted by a global third-party supplier. The breach exposed data belonging to 17.6 million users, making it one of Australia's largest data breaches by affected individuals.
records.sourceLabel: ABC News; Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The university reported unauthorised access to its Isilon storage platform between July 2023 and March 2024, with evidence of access to about 580 TB across 83 directories.
Qantas reported unauthorised access to a third-party customer service platform and exposure of customer data.

The university reported unauthorised access and download of historical personal information held in a code library, including records relating to former staff. The incident register reports: Confirmed 18 Dec 2025. Unauthorized persistent access to a legacy third-party IT code repository containing historical academic files. Exfiltrated student fields included full names; dates of birth; residential addresses; and phone numbers. No banking data was exposed; ACSC and NSW Privacy Commissioner notified. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical.
records.sourceLabel: The University of Sydney; Supplied incident register (unverified)

records.summary: Public reporting described data exposure affecting state education providers, TasTAFE, and universities; impact assessments were ongoing at publication.

A cyber attack on the sugar producer was publicly reported; the cited report says a ransomware group claimed responsibility and does not establish confirmed data theft or operational impact. The incident register reports: Major agricultural operator Mackay Sugar suffered a severe operational disruption after a targeted cyber attack hit its corporate and industrial network environments. The incident forced a proactive shutdown of automated manufacturing and IT systems; halting operations across multiple north Queensland sugar mills during the critical peak crushing season. While physical harvesting continued in some regions; the technical outage froze logistics scheduling; weighing; and refining processes. Cyber incident response teams were deployed to isolate the environment and initiate recovery from clean offline backups. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High.
records.sourceLabel: Australian Cyber Security Magazine; Actor claim: thegentlemen; Supplied incident register (unverified)

records.summary: Origin confirmed unauthorised access and disclosure of some customer data, including names, contact details, dates of birth and account information; its investigation was ongoing. The incident register reports: Origin Energy released its initial forensic scoping findings confirming that approximately 900;000 current and former customers had personal details exposed in the July security incident. Compromised data fields include full names; residential addresses; dates of birth; phone numbers; and utility account identifiers. Partial financial identifiers were also exfiltrated for a subset of users (including the last four digits of credit cards and last three digits of bank account numbers). Origin confirmed it first identified anomalous threat telemetry in early July but verified true system intrusion on July 22; initiating active victim notification workflows alongside the ACSC and OAIC. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical.

A CryptoLocker infection affected a production file server and made around 15,000 files inaccessible; the company restored them from backups without paying a ransom.
Ryuk ransomware disabled council systems, phones and email. The council said its investigation found no personal information had been compromised.
Inchcape confirmed an IT outage that disrupted systems. Contemporary reporting linked the event to RansomEXX, while the company's investigation into possible data compromise was ongoing.
An unauthorised party accessed a small number of Authorised Inspection Scheme user accounts containing personal information, including driver's licence details.

A ransomware attack led QUT to shut down multiple IT systems as a precaution; the university said some systems were compromised, while core student, staff and financial systems did not appear affected.
Nissan confirmed unauthorised access to IT servers affecting about 100,000 customers and staff in Australia and New Zealand; personal and confidential information was accessed.

A cyberattack disrupted IT systems at dealership locations, prompting the company to halt trading while it investigated the incident and its impact. The incident register reports: ASX-listed automotive dealership conglomerate Eagers Automotive executed an emergency trading halt following a systemic systems outage. Forensic analysis identified a targeted cyber incident that severely degraded sales processing frameworks. Incident type: DDoS; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Eagers Automotive, a Brisbane-based retail group and Australia's largest automotive dealer network, experienced a cyberattack in late December 2023 (publicly addressed in January 2024) that disrupted operations and resulted in unauthorized access to customer data. The LockBit 3.0 ransomware group claimed responsibility and threatened to publish stolen data.
records.sourceLabel: CarExpert; Actor claim: lockbit3; Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Sunshine Coast-based accounting; finance; and business advisory firm Poole Group was listed on the LockBit ransomware group's dark web leak site with a threat to release exfiltrated company data by October 25. Poole Group confirmed it experienced a cyber incident affecting part of its IT environment; engaged external cybersecurity specialists; and implemented immediate containment measures. The company notified the ACSC; OAIC; and Australian Taxation Office (ATO) as forensic investigations continue to evaluate the scope of exposed client and financial records. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High.

School administrators initiated an incident response protocol with external IT security specialists to assess the validity of the claims; secure internal networks; and determine whether any student or staff records were compromised. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High.

Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High.

Threat actors listed the Nepean and Hawkesbury-focused non-profit on their dark web leak portal; releasing sensitive exfiltrated records including passport scans and confidentiality agreements to prove system compromise. Thorndale Foundation acknowledged awareness of the claims and initiated incident response procedures alongside external IT security advisors to evaluate network integrity and assess data exposure. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High.

Threat actors claimed unauthorized network access and the exfiltration of sensitive corporate operational and financial data; threatening public release unless ransom demands were met. Sharp Office acknowledged the breach; stating an investigation was immediately launched alongside external forensic specialists to secure network environments; determine the scope of compromised data; and maintain customer continuity. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High.
records.sourceLabel: Actor claim: thegentlemen; Supplied incident register (unverified)

The incident register reports: Port Melbourne-based diesel engine and machinery management firm Macquarrie Corporation confirmed a third-party cybersecurity incident after being listed on the dark web leak portal of the Storm ransomware group. Threat actors gained unauthorized access to internal business systems via a compromised external technology provider. Storm subsequently published exfiltrated proof files including employee passport scans; death certificates; company correspondence; customer data; and credit listings. Macquarrie Corporation secured affected systems; engaged external cyber security and legal advisors; transitioned to alternative operational arrangements; and initiated direct notifications to impacted individuals alongside reporting to the ACSC and OAIC. Incident type: Supply Chain Attack; source-rated severity: High.
records.sourceLabel: Actor claim: Storm; Supplied incident register (unverified)

DigiGround initiated an immediate internal forensic investigation and confirmed it found no evidence of network compromise or data exposure. Technical monitoring; triage; and threat assessments remain ongoing. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High.

Threat actors published proof files to pressure the dealership into paying ransom demands. Agrimac has not publicly confirmed the breach or validated network compromise; with technical incident response; forensic triage; and log monitoring ongoing across its operataions. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High.

Storm initially listed the dealership on 24 August 2026; threatening data publication unless ransom demands were met. Sharp Motor Group confirmed that unauthorized access occurred via a third-party vendor environment rather than a direct breach of internal core network infrastructure. Sharp Motor Group initiated an incident response investigation alongside cybersecurity experts to assess supply chain connections; verify the nature of potential data exposure; and secure operational IT environments. Incident type: Supply Chain Attack; source-rated severity: High.

Cyber Daily reported the dark web listing; which emerged alongside multiple regional Australian targets listed by the group on the same day. Threat actors allege compromise of internal network systems and data exfiltration. Westco Motors has not publicly verified the ransomware claims; with technical threat assessments; log monitoring; and incident response investigations ongoing. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.
records.sourceLabel: Actor claim: Storm; Supplied incident register (unverified)

Cyber Daily reported that no formal proof files or initial data samples were immediately published on the leak page.
