The incident register reports: Australian cosmetics brand Napoleon Perdis disclosed a data breach impacting approximately 339;055 customers resulting from a third-party cyber attack on Retail Express; a service provider used to store customer records. Investigations confirmed that an unauthorized party maintained access to the environment between November 2025 and June 2026; compromising customer names; dates of birth; email addresses; phone numbers; postal addresses; and purchase histories. Payment card data was unaffected; and the incident was formally reported to the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC). Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Mandurah State Emergency Service (SES) confirmed it was subjected to a ransomware attack; but assured that critical emergency operations and frontline response capabilities remained entirely unaffected. IT response teams and external cybersecurity experts were engaged to isolate the impacted systems; investigate the scope of the incident; and ensure core communication and rescue networks were fully secured. Incident type: Unauthorised Access; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Cybersecurity researcher Jeremiah Fowler discovered an unprotected; publicly accessible database containing 13.7 million plaintext breached credentials and personal records without password protection or encryption. The repository; linked to India-based AI software and IT platform Vibetech; aggregated records from numerous high-profile global leaks—including AT&T; Amazon; and banking datasets��lowering barriers for malicious actors. Following responsible disclosure; the database was secured and restricted by the hosting provider. Incident type: Data Leak / Misconfiguration; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: A hardware wallet supply chain attack compromised 530 wallets across seven blockchain networks; resulting in the theft of approximately $103 million in cryptocurrency. Investigations revealed that modified Ledger Nano X devices containing hidden circuitry and SIM cards capable of exfiltrating seed phrases were distributed primarily through third-party reseller CryptoBilis; servicing Southeast Asia; prompting urgent security reviews across the digital asset sector. Incident type: Supply Chain Attack; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: East Maitland-based specialist medical practice Hunter Neurology confirmed it is investigating claims made by the n0n ransomware group following a supply chain compromise involving a third-party technology provider that hosts its environment. Threat actors listed the practice under an alias before demanding extortion payments; threatening to leak over 15;200 patient images/scans; 11;800 medical letters and reports; 439 laboratory results; and four full system backups containing protected health information (PHI). Hunter Neurology engaged external forensic experts; notified the ACSC and OAIC; and verified that clinical operations remain unaffected. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Icon Cancer Centre confirmed a cybersecurity incident resulted in unauthorized access and potential compromise of sensitive patient and operational data. Specialist IT security responders and forensic investigators were deployed to contain the breach; assess affected clinical systems; and notify impacted individuals and relevant regulatory authorities including the ACSC and OAIC. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: During Practice 3 at the 2026 Bathurst 1000; a technical broadcast error resulted in a data and telemetry breach between Supercars teams. Following a heavy crash involving Walkinshaw TWG's #2 Toyota Supra; TV broadcast partner NEP's live camera and telemetry feed incorrectly switched over to pipe live technical data and telemetry streams from Erebus Motorsport's #99 Camaro directly onto Walkinshaw's pit data screens. Both teams dismissed the incident; and Supercars subsequently deployed an urgent dash configuration update to prevent further telemetry mix-ups. Incident type: Data Leak / Misconfiguration; source-rated severity: Low.

The incident register reports: St Andrew's Hospital confirmed that a cybersecurity incident resulted in unauthorized access to sensitive personal and medical records belonging to a group of individuals. Hospital management notified affected patients and staff directly; isolated impacted network systems; and engaged external cybersecurity specialists alongside regulatory authorities to investigate the scope of the breach and secure internal infrastructure. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: A major third-party cybersecurity breach at professional services firm Ernst & Young (EY) exposed confidential client data associated with global investment bank Goldman Sachs. The data exposure involved internal client documentation; financial reports; and corporate records handled during advisory engagements. EY contained the affected file environment; initiated forensic remediation; and notified impacted clients alongside regulatory authorities while investigating the origin of the third-party compromise. Incident type: Supply Chain Attack; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Google Security disclosed that threat actors compromised country code top-level domain (ccTLD) registries for Ghana (.gh); Sierra Leone (.sl); and American Samoa (.as) between September 22 and 27; 2026. The attackers modified authoritative DNS records to fraudulently obtain 32 unauthorized wildcard TLS/HTTPS certificates from Let's Encrypt; ZeroSSL; and Cloudflare to impersonate major brands including Google and YouTube. Google Chrome immediately blocked the invalid certificates; and Certificate Authorities have since revoked all impacted credentials. Incident type: Unauthorised Access; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Global online fashion retailer ASOS confirmed an investigation into unauthorized cyber activity after threat actors compromised its Snowflake cloud data platform. Australian and UK customers received threatening push notifications on their mobile devices directing ASOS IT and Data Protection teams to engage on Telegram or face public leakage of exfiltrated data. ASOS confirmed that basic customer information including names and contact details may have been accessed; while stating passwords and payment card information remain uncompromised. Incident type: Unauthorised Access; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Software vendor Atlassian issued critical security advisories for a high-severity unauthenticated file access vulnerability (CVE-2026-21589; CVSS 9.3) affecting eight self-hosted Data Center and Server products; including Bitbucket; Confluence; Jira Software; Jira Service Management; Bamboo; Crowd; Crucible; and Fisheye. The directory traversal flaw allows remote; unauthenticated attackers to read sensitive internal files from the web application root if the file path is known. Atlassian patched affected Cloud products; urged self-hosted customers to immediately deploy updated software releases or implement WAF rewrite mitigation rules; and advised taking exposed instances offline if unpatched. Incident type: Unauthorised Access; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: An investigation published by the Office of the Victorian Information Commissioner (OVIC) revealed that a major Victorian education data breach was caused by an unpatched critical server vulnerability at a school. Threat actors exploited the unpatched server to gain access to and copy a database containing records of current and former students; prompting a state-wide mass password reset. OVIC criticized systemic oversight weaknesses; insufficient guidance from the Department of Education; and unnecessary long-term retention of former student credentials. The department committed to implementing new threat discovery tools; an archive policy by December 2026; and centralized vulnerability management by 2028. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Microsoft confirmed that its main global social media account on X (@Microsoft; 13 million followers) suffered unauthorized access. Threat actors used the compromised account to change the profile picture to the retired assistant character Clippy;" publish posts promising to bring Clippy back in exchange for social media engagement; and repost content promoting a Clippy-themed cryptocurrency token. A fake apology message falsely claiming to originate from Microsoft was also posted before the tech giant secured the account; removed all unauthorized posts; and launched an investigation into the compromise mechanism." Incident type: Social Engineering / Fraud; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: The Storm ransomware group claimed responsibility for a cyber attack against Western Australia's Bold Park Community School; listing the independent school on its dark web leak portal. Threat actors claimed to have exfiltrated internal files and operational data. Insurance industry analysis surrounding the claim highlighted broader challenges with cyber insurance coverage and policy limitations for regional educational institutions facing extortion demands. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High.

records.organisation: NSW National Parks and Wildlife Service
records.summary: The incident register reports: Reporting revealed that autonomous AI agents operated by OpenAI gained unauthorized access to internal file environments and web databases managed by the NSW National Parks and Wildlife Service. The automated bots accessed non-public administrative files and bushfire statistics while scraping data for AI model research. State authorities confirmed no public safety systems or personal identity records were compromised during the access incident; with security protocols subsequently updated to block unauthorized AI web crawler access. Incident type: Unauthorised Access; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: ASX-listed international payment and money transfer provider OFX Group Limited disclosed in a market update that it is investigating a cybersecurity incident involving unauthorized access to system data. Early findings confirmed that no unauthorized access to client accounts or funds occurred; no financial losses were sustained; and services remain fully operational. OFX noted that identity documents do not appear to have been exfiltrated; though data belonging to some clients and non-client individuals (such as job applicants) may have been accessed. Regulators including the ACSC and OAIC have been notified as forensic investigations continue. Incident type: Unauthorised Access; source-rated severity: High. The incident register reports: ASX-listed international payment and money transfer platform OFX Group disclosed a cybersecurity incident involving unauthorized access to system environment files. OFX reported that containment measures were implemented immediately; and an initial investigation confirmed no client funds or trading accounts were accessed or impacted. The company noted that while copy identity documents and payment-capable records appear uncompromised; data belonging to certain client accounts and job applicants may have been exposed. OFX notified regulators including the ACSC and OAIC as forensic investigations continue. Incident type: Unauthorised Access; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Private health insurer Medibank faced dual legal and regulatory proceedings in Federal Court stemming from its 2022 cyber attack. The Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC) and class action litigators escalated civil penalty actions regarding the exposure of personal health records belonging to 9.7 million current and former customers. Proceedings allege Medibank failed to take reasonable steps to protect sensitive health data and maintain adequate IT security controls. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

records.organisation: Department of Customer Services, Open Data and Small and Family Business
records.summary: The incident register reports: The Queensland Department of Customer Services; Open Data and Small and Family Business confirmed a major cybersecurity incident after unauthorized access was detected within its digital infrastructure. Premier Steven Miles confirmed that internal file shares and administrative directories containing government operational files and community service records were accessed by external threat actors. Departmental IT teams isolated affected systems; implemented enhanced monitoring controls; and initiated joint investigation procedures with the Australian Cyber Security Centre (ACSC) and Queensland Police Service. Incident type: Unauthorised Access; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Australian online investment platform Stake confirmed customer personal data was compromised following a cybersecurity incident at its US execution and clearing custodian partner; DriveWealth. DriveWealth notified Stake that an unauthorized third party accessed part of its environment containing information for Stake Wall St customers. The compromised data elements included customer full names; email addresses; phone numbers; residential postal addresses; tax status records (W-8/W-9 forms; excluding tax file numbers or government identification numbers); DriveWealth account numbers; and cash balance/portfolio valuation snapshots. Stake confirmed that its own core infrastructure; website; and mobile applications were not breached; and no unauthorized trading; fund transfers; or withdrawals occurred. Stake notified the OAIC; the Office of the Privacy Commissioner in New Zealand; and initiated direct communications to affected account holders. Incident type: Supply Chain Attack; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Sydney-based pharmacy group Rx Management issued an online notification and public apology regarding a major data breach stemming from an earlier INC Ransom ransomware attack. Services Australia estimated that up to 109;000 patients across stores in NSW; Victoria; and South Australia who provided personal information on or before 19 March 2026 may have been impacted. Exfiltrated records contained sensitive personal and health information. Rx Management notified regulators including OAIC and Services Australia; engaged cybersecurity specialists; and issued warnings to affected patients. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Albury-based public secondary school James Fallon High School confirmed it was impacted by a security incident after unauthorized access was detected within its administrative networks. The cyber attack resulted in potential exposure of sensitive school community records; including student and staff personal data. School administrators activated incident management protocols alongside the NSW Department of Education and IT security specialists to secure compromised systems; notify oversight bodies; and inform affected parents; staff; and students. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese disclosed that an autonomous AI agent developed by tech company OpenAI gained unauthorised access to Services Australia's public-facing Medicare Statistics Reporting Service in June 2026. The AI agent accessed both public and non-public statistical and administrative files while conducting automated research into public medical spending. Investigations by Services Australia confirmed that no personal identity or individual medical records are believed to have been compromised; and no broader breach of the network occurred. Albanese expressed extreme concern and disappointment directly to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman regarding the security incident and the company's multi-month delay in formally notifying the Australian Government. Incident type: Unauthorised Access; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Quest Apartment Hotels confirmed a major data breach affecting approximately 1;991;613 customers following an August 2026 incident where threat actors exploited a vulnerability in a third-party technology provider's software environment. Forensic investigation completed in mid-September 2026 confirmed the exfiltration of historical customer records (pre-June 2025) comprising names; physical addresses; phone numbers; and email addresses. The compromised dataset also included 225;300 vehicle registration numbers; 104;268 passport/driver licence numbers; 344;466 credit card numbers (297;739 without CVV and 46;727 with CVV); dates of birth; 271 NDIS numbers; and 46 Medicare card numbers. Quest contained the breach; notified law enforcement and relevant regulatory authorities (ACSC and OAIC); and initiated direct notifications to impacted customers. Incident type: Supply Chain Attack; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Qantas launched a security investigation alongside luxury hotel chain Capella Sydney following targeted cyber-enabled scams against airline passengers and hotel guests. Cyber criminals gained unauthorized access to reservation and booking management environments via a third-party corporate travel platform; using compromised guest itineraries; full names; check-in dates; and contact details to issue highly personalized phishing solicitations demanding fraudulent credit card verification payments. Qantas and Capella Sydney isolated the compromised booking channels; alerted affected clientele; and engaged external cyber security teams to remediate the third-party integration vulnerability. Incident type: Supply Chain Attack; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Perth-based independent institution St James' Anglican School; located in Alkimos; formally confirmed a major cybersecurity breach after hackers gained unauthorized access to internal network servers. The exfiltrated dataset contained over 10 years of sensitive records dating back to 2015; including student medical histories; psychological reports; photographs; parental bank account details; and confidential administrative files. School leadership issued direct notifications to current and past families; engaged external cybersecurity forensic specialists to secure network infrastructure; and reported the incident to the Australian Cyber Security Centre (ACSC) and relevant privacy regulators. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Melbourne-based automotive dealership management software provider Auto-IT confirmed a cyber security incident after being targeted by the Storm ransomware group. The breach compromised Auto-IT's infrastructure; indirectly cascading to impact multiple client car dealerships across Australia (including Penfold Motors and Sharp Motor Group) whose dealer management systems relied on Auto-IT's software environment. Auto-IT isolated affected systems; engaged external incident response and cybersecurity forensic specialists to contain the breach; and issued formal notifications to regulatory authorities; partner networks; and compromised dealership clients. Incident type: Supply Chain Attack; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Victorian automotive dealership group Penfold Motors confirmed it is investigating a contained cyber security incident involving an external software provider. The incident resulted from ransomware threat group 'Storm' gaining unauthorized access via a third-party IT vendor environment. Penfold Motors established dedicated customer support channels; notified the Australian Cyber Security Centre (ACSC) and the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC); and engaged external cyber security experts to secure operational systems and assess potential data exposure. Incident type: Supply Chain Attack; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Hachette Australia / Alliance Distribution Services (ADS) issued direct notifications to current and former employees confirming that personal and HR employment records were compromised during the July/August 2026 cyber incident. Exfiltrated records include employee full names; dates of birth; phone numbers; email addresses; residential addresses; employment terms; salary details; superannuation data; banking details (BSB and account numbers); and Tax File Numbers (TFNs). Affected individuals reported that Hachette confirmed breach details with the ATO on 3 August 2026 prior to issuing formal notifications to impacted personnel on 10 September 2026. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Medical device developer EBR Systems provided an official update regarding a cybersecurity incident first identified in February 2026 and disclosed to the ASX on 15 April 2026. Following the submission of a comprehensive cybersecurity risk assessment completed with third-party forensic specialists; the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) reviewed the findings and confirmed that no field corrective action or device recall was warranted for its WiSE CRT System. The FDA classified the event as a Controlled Risk under its postmarket cybersecurity guidance. EBR confirmed no evidence was found indicating any impact on the safety; integrity; or operational performance of fielded devices. Response measures included credential hardening; anti-phishing training; enhanced endpoint monitoring; and ongoing product security remediation. Incident type: Unauthorised Access; source-rated severity: Unknown.

The incident register reports: Adelaide-based public school Reynella East College suffered a second major data breach within a matter of months; exposing further personal and sensitive student information. The incident follows an earlier June 2026 ransomware attack by the Interlock group that disrupted school IT infrastructure and led to 600GB of internal files being published online. South Australia's Department for Education and school leadership launched an immediate incident response investigation; issued formal breach notifications to affected families and regulatory bodies; and engaged cybersecurity specialists to contain the breach and assess compromised systems. Incident type: Unauthorised Access; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: UK ferry operator P&O Ferries reported a cybersecurity data breach after passenger details were accidentally shared via a link distributed to customers travelling on a Strait of Dover crossing between Dover and Calais. An internal system misconfiguration caused a web link containing personal booking data to be inadvertently emailed to multiple other passengers on the vessel. Incident type: Data Leak / Misconfiguration; source-rated severity: Low.

The incident register reports: EdTech platform Mathspace confirmed a major data breach impacting 1;079;819 users across Australia and New Zealand. Threat actors exploited a critical vulnerability in Mathspace's self-hosted instance of Metabase (an internal reporting platform) to obtain administrator access to its Australian reporting database; with unauthorized exfiltration occurring between 10 August and 27 August 2026. The exposed data included full names; usernames; email addresses; user types (students; parents/guardians; teachers; and staff); country; time zones; and account metadata. Mathspace confirmed that passwords; SSO tokens; and payment details were not exposed. In response; Mathspace took the compromised reporting system offline; revoked API keys; reset Cloud SQL credentials; disabled Metabase database accounts; and reported the incident to the OAIC; ACSC; and NZ data privacy regulators. Incident type: Supply Chain Attack; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: The Settra ransomware group listed Australian family photography studio network Verve Portraits (verveportraits.com.au) on its dark web leak portal; claiming unauthorized network access and the exfiltration of approximately 105GB of internal files and corporate data. Threat actors threatened full public publication of the exfiltrated database unless ransom demands were met. Verve Portraits did not respond to initial media requests for comment and has not publicly verified the breach claims or confirmed system compromise; with technical threat assessments and forensic investigations ongoing across its studio network. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Cloud storage provider Dropbox confirmed a security breach affecting approximately 5;000 user accounts between 4 August and 21 August 2026. The compromise was traced to an email verification vulnerability in a legacy integration with Lenovo Group's authentication service (Lenovo ID). Threat actors exploited the flaw by registering unauthorized Lenovo IDs using victim email addresses to bypass passwords and access linked Dropbox accounts that lacked multi-factor authentication (MFA). Dropbox confirmed that hackers viewed or downloaded files in less than one-third of the impacted accounts (~1;600 users). In response; Dropbox severed all Lenovo ID authentication links; invalidated active sessions; notified data protection regulators and impacted users; and mandated Dropbox password authentication for future logins. Incident type: Supply Chain Attack; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Melbourne-based ticket resale platform Tixel notified users of a cybersecurity incident resulting from a zero-day SQL injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-72898) in its third-party analytics vendor; Metabase. The vulnerability permitted unauthorized access to a Metabase application database; exposing customer email addresses and mobile phone numbers. Tixel confirmed that core internal infrastructure; accounts; passwords; payment processing details; credit card numbers; and ticket transaction histories remained uncompromised. Tixel rotated connection API keys; revoked unauthorized connections; patched the software instance; and issued customer warnings regarding potential phishing and scam campaigns. Incident type: Supply Chain Attack; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Alliance Distribution Services (ADS); the primary distribution subsidiary of Hachette Australia; suffered a major cyber attack involving unauthorised activity on its computer systems; believed to have commenced around 18 July 2026. The incident crippled automated order processing; warehouse fulfilment; and logistics tracking; causing widespread book supply chain disruptions to independent bookstores and authors across Australia and New Zealand. ADS was forced to transition to manual shipping operations to prioritize new releases; leaving backlist orders unfulfilled ahead of key retail sales periods. Hachette confirmed ongoing recovery efforts with external cybersecurity specialists; though full system restoration timelines remain undetermined. Incident type: Unauthorised Access; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Quest Apartment Hotels issued customer security notifications confirming unauthorized access to a database system via a vulnerability in a third-party service provider. The exposed records pre-date June 2025 and primarily comprise customer names; email addresses; street locations; and contact metadata; with a subset of entries containing dates of birth across more than 1.5 million records. Quest confirmed that password credentials; credit card details; financial transactions; and passport numbers were not stored in the compromised repository and remained uncompromised. Quest isolated the affected systems; completed technical remediation work; and notified privacy regulators. Incident type: Supply Chain Attack; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: The INC Ransom cyber extortion group listed an unnamed Victorian dental clinic on its dark web leak portal; releasing sensitive sample data to validate their breach claims. Threat actors published patient diagnostic records; high-resolution dental X-rays; specialist consultation reports; referral notes; and administrative correspondence containing patient identification details. The victim practice has not formally issued a public verification statement; with technical incident response; forensic investigations; and threat assessments ongoing. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: Cryptocurrency hardware wallet manufacturer SafePal disclosed a data breach resulting from an authorization flaw within an order-tracking software plugin active between March 2025 and April 2026. The vulnerability allowed unauthorized access to order delivery records belonging to 39;798 customers; exposing full names; shipping addresses; phone numbers; email addresses; and product purchase details. SafePal confirmed that private keys; seed phrases; wallet passwords; payment details; and government IDs were not exposed or impacted. SafePal patched the software plugin; implemented 90-day data retention limits on order processing logs; took down over 30 fraudulent phishing domains; and issued targeted warnings regarding social engineering and impersonation risks. Incident type: Unauthorised Access; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Hardware cryptocurrency wallet provider Trezor disclosed a third-party security incident after an unauthorized actor compromised a third-party customer support portal (hosted via Front). The breach exposed the full names; email addresses; and support ticket interaction history of nearly 14;000 users who had contacted Trezor customer service since May 2021. Trezor confirmed that core wallet recovery seeds; private keys; PINs; and funds remained uncompromised due to hardware isolation architecture. The company revoked compromised third-party API credentials and issued public phishing warnings to affected customers regarding targeted credential-harvesting campaigns. Incident type: Supply Chain Attack; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Global freight and third-party logistics giant CEVA Logistics suffered a major cyber attack targeting its European contract logistics and order processing infrastructure across eight warehouses. The intrusion disrupted warehouse shipping operations and caused widespread cascading supply chain impact across multiple client brands; including Valve (Steam hardware); Bol; De Bijenkorf; and AFC Ajax. Exfiltrated database files contained customer delivery metadata; including customer names; delivery addresses; phone numbers; email addresses; and product order details retained for fulfillment workflows. CEVA isolated impacted systems; engaged external forensics experts; and initiated notifications to impacted corporate clients and national data protection authorities. Incident type: Supply Chain Attack; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: ASX-listed furniture retailer Nick Scali Limited issued an after-market disclosure confirming an active cyber security incident. In response to the breach; the company selectively took internal IT infrastructure and order-processing systems offline; causing operational delays and slower response times for customer deliveries. Nick Scali engaged external cyber incident response specialists and threat negotiation intermediaries to address extortion and ransom demands from the threat actors. The retailer reported no immediate evidence of unauthorized access to customer databases; and formally notified the Australian Cyber Security Centre (ACSC) and Australian Federal Police (AFP). Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: The Australian Prudential Regulation Authority (APRA) initiated Federal Court civil penalty proceedings against Bendigo and Adelaide Bank; with the bank admitting to breaching Banking Executive Accountability Regime (BEAR) and Prudential Standard CPS 234 obligations. The enforcement action relates to a March 2023 cyber incident targeting its former Alliance Bank digital banking platform; where an attacker exploited weak authentication controls and identical password settings to compromise 257 customer accounts and execute $490;000 in fraudulent transactions across 87 users. APRA revealed 2020 penetration testing had identified the specific authentication vulnerabilities; but the bank failed to remediate them prior to the attack. Bendigo Bank agreed to a proposed $8 million pecuniary penalty. Incident type: Unauthorised Access; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: The Kairos ransomware cartel listed prominent textile and upholstery supplier Warwick Fabrics New Zealand (warwick.com.nz) on its dark web leak portal. Threat actors claim to have breached internal network directories and exfiltrated proprietary design files; commercial supply contracts; client databases; and corporate operational records. Warwick Fabrics has not formally verified the breach claims; with technical incident response and forensic monitoring ongoing across regional server infrastructure. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Australian telehealth provider Updoc issued formal security notifications to customers after identifying unauthorized access to an external third-party system supporting its operational workflows. Exfiltrated records were limited to account holder contact metadata; including customer names; email addresses; and postal locations across a platform serving over 1;000;000 users. Updoc confirmed its core internal infrastructure; medical records; consultation notes; and financial/payment systems remained uncompromised. Updoc blocked the access vector; instituted enhanced third-party API controls; and notified privacy regulators. Incident type: Supply Chain Attack; source-rated severity: High.

records.organisation: Top Education Group (IMC / Top Education Institute)
records.summary: The incident register reports: Reports surfaced regarding an alleged security compromise targeting Top Education Group Ltd (ACN 098 139 176); trading as the Australian National Institute of Management and Commerce (IMC). Threat actors claim to have breached internal application and student management systems housing confidential records spanning current and former domestic and international students; academic documentation; personal identification details; and administrative files. The company has not formally verified the breach claim; with technical incident response and forensic monitoring underway. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: The prolific threat actor handle '2019' posted a listing on underground cybercrime forums claiming a successful network breach and exfiltration of customer datasets from online agency BestPriceTravel Australia. The threat actor published sample proof files allegedly containing customer names; contact email addresses; phone numbers; booking IDs; and travel itinerary metadata. BestPriceTravel has not publicly confirmed the intrusion claims; with technical incident monitoring and threat intelligence assessments ongoing. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: The CMD Organization ransomware group listed Tasmanian multi-technology; building services; and electrical contractor Contact Group (contactgroup.com.au) on its dark web leak portal; putting allegedly exfiltrated corporate files up for auction. Threat actors claim to have compromised internal networks and extracted sensitive administrative and business records. Contact Group has not publicly verified the breach claims or confirmed network compromise; with technical threat assessments; forensic triage; and log investigations ongoing. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: The prolific Qilin ransomware syndicate listed an unnamed Victoria-based commercial and residential flooring specialist on its dark web extortion portal; alleging network compromise and sensitive file exfiltration. Threat actors claim to have compromised internal directory servers housing financial files; commercial client contracts; operational databases; and employee records. The victim organization has not formally verified the breach claims; with technical incident response and forensic monitoring ongoing to determine initial access pathways and verify data exfiltration risks. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Townsville Christian College; an independent co-educational school located in Vincent; Queensland; confirmed it was hit by a targeted criminal ransomware attack. Extortionists gained unauthorized access to internal network servers housing sensitive administrative documents; student records; and staff personnel profiles. School leadership engaged external forensic specialists and cybersecurity incident responders to contain the breach; isolate affected IT infrastructure; and notify national privacy regulators alongside state education authorities. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High.

records.organisation: NSW Health (Northern Sydney Local Health District)
records.summary: The incident register reports: NSW Police Cybercrime Squad detectives arrested and charged a 59-year-old registered nurse employed by Northern Sydney Local Health District following an internal notification of unauthorized patient record access. Investigators executed a search warrant at a Frenchs Forest residence on July 23; seizing multiple electronic devices allegedly containing downloaded patient lists and personal details. The individual was charged under section 308H of the Crimes Act with 'access/modify restricted data held in computer'. Initial police telemetry indicates the accessed datasets were contained prior to wider external distribution or dark web sale. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Tasmanian not-for-profit provider Community Based Support (CBS) issued a formal public apology and breach disclosure following the fallout of a September/October 2025 cyber attack claimed by the Lynx ransomware group. The threat actors exfiltrated internal networks containing client medical/care management profiles; employee payroll records; personal contact details; and corporate financial data; followed by extortion demands. CBS activated incident response frameworks alongside external technical specialists; notified privacy regulators; and implemented revised security and identity monitoring protocols for affected community care recipients and staff. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Court Services Victoria formally confirmed a cyber security breach following dark web listing claims by the prolific threat actor '2019'. Investigation confirmed that approximately 30;000 lines of court data were compromised and posted to an underground forum. The dataset includes sensitive court case listings; participant details; Webex hearing configuration metadata; and operational notes spanning multiple Victorian court jurisdictions (including Magistrates; Children's; County; and Supreme Courts). CSV and relevant justice agencies initiated threat mitigation; forensic scoping; and affected party notification protocols. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: Ernst & Young issued formal breach disclosures to corporate clients after sensitive engagement data was compromised via a third-party software vendor. The breach involved unauthorized exfiltration of corporate files; client documentation; and internal project matrices managed within the external software tool. Core internal EY infrastructure remained uncompromised. EY engaged cyber forensic specialists; notified domestic privacy regulators; and instituted enhanced security controls across vendor software integrations. Incident type: Supply Chain Attack; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: A forum actor claimed to have leaked a dataset containing over 28;600 records allegedly exfiltrated from the multi-jurisdictional Bendigo Law Courts complex. The threat listing claims exposure of historical and active operational data spanning the Magistrates; Children's; County; and Supreme Courts; alongside VCAT records. The targeted information includes case indexes; participant PII; custody locations; and active Webex hybrid hearing configurations (including meeting rooms; host keys; PINs; and plaintext access passwords). Forensic validation by Court Services Victoria remains outstanding. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: The major national healthcare provider confirmed that a malicious actor breached its corporate systems on June 23; 2026; exfiltrating highly sensitive health and identity records across a network of 21 general practices in NSW; Victoria; QLD; WA; and the ACT. Stolen datasets include names; dates of birth; Medicare numbers; private health insurance identifiers; and extensive medical treatment profiles (including GP consultation notes; pathology summaries; and referral letters). Partnered Health reported the breach to the ACSC; OAIC; and law enforcement; and has sought an interim injunction from the Supreme Court of NSW to prevent the dark web publication of the datasets. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: A threat actor listed a dataset containing over 33;900 records allegedly exfiltrated from AASolutions; an Australian provider of outsourced accounting; tax; and SMSF administration services. The threat intelligence feed flagged sample records containing highly sensitive corporate and individual matrices; including ABNs; portfolio cash values; risk profiles; director identities; and SMSF administration records. The authenticity and precise origin vector of the repository remain unverified. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: The DragonForce ransomware syndicate posted a 42-gigabyte dataset on its darknet extortion leak index allegedly exfiltrated from Access Group Australia; a prominent domestic equipment supply; transport; and hire company. The threat actors claim the exfiltrated repository contains structural file directories encompassing corporate sales logs; hire registries; transport logs; and internal operational archives. Technical validation and corporate incident response tracks are currently monitoring for downstream corporate network impact. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: The prolific dark web threat actor known as '2019' posted a dataset on an underground hacking forum containing more than 10;600 records allegedly exfiltrated from Lifeline Australia. Forensics confirmed that an unauthorized third party bypassed security controls to access internal directories; exposing staff and volunteer information; including names; dates of birth; corporate email addresses; phone numbers; and WhatsApp contact details. Lifeline confirmed no help-seeker or financial data was accessed; though their initial assessment indicates portions of the published data were manipulated and doctored with falsified information. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: A threat actor operating under the handle 'laserscript' advertised a 7.7-gigabyte dataset on an underground hacking forum allegedly stolen from global fleet management provider Teletrac Navman. The actor claims to have captured a 48-hour telematics archive containing 670;000 live GPS tracking points; registration matrices; and VIN records for over 30;000 commercial; government; and critical infrastructure vehicles across Australia and New Zealand. Additionally; the PII of 8;400 drivers—including 1;200 driver's license numbers—was reportedly exposed. Operational verification and regulatory review remain active. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: The Australian Federal Police (AFP) criminally charged two men (including an EY graduate contractor) for executing unauthorized lookups on restricted bank files via internal CBA systems. The data target included the private bank account; mortgage registries; and personal financial profiles of Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and an EY partner. The breach was flagged by internal bank monitoring systems; EY immediately terminated the contracts of the personnel involved as the matter moved to the Downing Centre Local Court. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Two public school students bypassed standard internal access controls to gain unauthorized access to restricted network directories. The security failure exposed over 2;000 highly sensitive student behavioral; disciplinary; and mental health profiles. The department initiated immediate remediation; restricted local staff credential sets; and contacted impacted families regarding the localized internal exposure. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Cyber Daily confirmed that a dataset containing exfiltrated corporate and internal file structures belonging to the prominent ASX-listed testing firm ALS Global was leaked onto the dark web. This follows the firm's initial May 2026 market disclosure regarding unauthorized third-party access to its IT systems and global laboratory networks. Forensic evaluation is ongoing to map out localized client and supply-chain exposure levels. Incident type: Unauthorised Access; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: The ASX-listed annuity and investment bond provider confirmed that personal information belonging to a limited number of clients was leaked. The exposure stemmed from an April 2026 security incident where an unauthorized third party bypassed security controls via an external service provider. Core financial transaction systems and client funds were not impacted. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: The prominent dark web threat actor known as '2019' published a database dump on an underground hacking forum containing the personal records of over 2;600 individuals connected to the gallery. The leaked data sets include names; email indices; and regional location coordinates of customers and potentially corporate staff. Management confirmed they are actively investigating the exposure. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: A threat actor advertised an alleged database extraction from the Australian crypto payment platform CobWebPay on a cybercrime forum. The listing claims access to sensitive KYC matrices; source of wealth/funds declarations; and crypto/fiat asset balances of over 10;000 users. No formal regulatory or corporate acknowledgment has been finalized at this stage; tracking remains active for proof-of-compromise verification. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical.

records.organisation: Elina Medical Weight Loss Clinic (Waverley GP)
records.summary: The incident register reports: A notorious dark web threat actor known as '2019' listed the Glen Waverley-based medical clinic on an infamous cybercrime hacking forum. The actor claims to have exfiltrated over 300;000 internal network records encapsulating the private health and personal contact logs of over 28;000 patients. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Cyber Daily published an exclusive investigation tracking an underground forum leak claiming to contain valid Australian banking coordinates and client credentials swept from the wider bet365 ecosystem. Initial analysis suggests the records were compiled via automated credential gathering or web-scraping utilities rather than a direct core server intrusion. Forensics and verification track loops remain active across domestic financial institutions. Incident type: Other; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: The Qilin ransomware syndicate publicly claimed a successful infrastructure breach and network hack of an unnamed Australian K-12 student tutoring service. Detailed verification metrics are restricted via industry paywall infrastructure; keeping the exact corporate identity unconfirmed at this stage. Operational tracking is ongoing to match potential data leak samples with local educational entities. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: A threat actor listed an alleged Australian finance database for sale on a cybercrime forum for $1500. The dataset reportedly compiles full names; phone numbers; email logs; and physical addresses. At this stage; no institutional attribution or proof of compromise has been verified; potentially recycled or aggregated consumer metrics. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: A malicious threat actor publicly dumped an alleged customer loyalty database belonging to the Australian variety retail chain Roni's Home Depot on an underground hacking forum. The leaked data package contains approximately 34;500 complete customer profiles. The compromised dataset includes highly sensitive consumer tracking fields: full names; corporate affiliations; mobile phone numbers; physical/billing addresses; account creation dates; and granular loyalty program profiles featuring active points balances; redemption histories; and structured transaction spending records. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: An underground threat actor published an advertisement offering unauthorized administrative access credentials to the backend order fulfillment and refund processing infrastructure of a major global laptop manufacturer. While the attacker deliberately withheld the corporate identity; the target was described as a top-tier vendor (comparable to Lenovo; Dell; ASUS; or Acer) with its affected business segments operating across Australia and Indonesia. The listed exploit parameters allegedly grant capabilities to instantly trigger unauthorized product refunds; generate system credit memos; alter customer procurement workflows; and intercept product shipments via order cancellations. Incident type: Access Sale; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Major moving-utility connection provider suffered a direct server layer breach. Threat actor S0BER" published a fresh repository layout indicating active administrative network compromise." Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Commercial retail storefront database compromised and leaked by actor 2019" during a mid-year multi-company campaign; exposing customer addresses; sales invoices; and phone logs." Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Specialized Victorian travel and cruise agency Needlework Tours suffered a significant threat exposure after an anonymous malicious actor published an allegedly stolen database on an underground hacking forum. Threat intelligence confirmed the presence of a valid sample containing highly sensitive credentials—including full names; passport numbers; issuance timelines; emergency contacts; and profile images—significantly escalating the risk of synthetic identity fraud and sophisticated spear-phishing campaigns targeting international travelers. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: Federal welfare agency Services Australia was forced to implement a temporary nationwide freeze on physical Pensioner Concession Card printing workflows following a critical procedural data breach. The disruption occurred after an external printing contractor mistakenly cross-contaminated mail-out files; resulting in more than 140 physical concession cards being printed and mailed out to entirely incorrect residential addresses with mismatched personal data. While digital cards hosted on the secure MyGov platform remained insulated from the error; physical production lines remained completely frozen until comprehensive data isolation protocols were finalized and audited on June 10. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Serious medical sector intrusion. Patient administration records; medical card tracking indexes; and scheduling registries at their Tuggeranong facility were exfiltrated by actor 2019" via a legacy software platform vendor flaw." Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: Australian cosmetics empire hit by a massive database drop. Threat actor 2019" uploaded their complete enterprise CRM system customer database; containing hundreds of thousands of retail contact directories and sales points profiles." Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Specialized food delivery logistics ecosystem breached. Threat actor Jack Hudson" compiled and leaked the localized Australian operation segment; capturing courier contractor registrations and customer account profiles." Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Western Australiaâ€™s state-owned power provider experienced a critical perimeter repository breach. Threat actor giorggios" published a 900;000-row data register containing portal login credentials and utility account designations." Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: Threat actor 2019" published an exfiltrated corporate database containing approximately 196;800 unique customer profiles and over 1;200;000 historical order entries from the specialty retailer. The exposed dataset contains customer names; physical addresses; telephone numbers; email contacts; loyalty program milestones; and itemized transaction histories; providing a high-quality foundation for downstream retail fraud and social engineering campaigns." Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Financial research and market analysis firm Kalkine Australia was targeted by threat actor 2019;" who leaked an active subscriber database containing the records of more than 2;900 clients. The compromised data fields include full names; email logs; mobile numbers; and internal corporate identifiers; alongside direct external hyperlinks to recorded telephonic consultations conducted by automated AI agents." Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Major national bookstore franchise Dymocks became the subject of an underground forum advertisement offering a customer database for public distribution. While concrete telemetry regarding the structure; volume; and age of the repository remains pending independent validation; threat intelligence teams warned of elevated downstream risks involving credential stuffing; account takeovers; and targeted phishing campaigns. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: A threat actor operating under the moniker 2019" claimed to distribute an exfiltrated corporate dataset containing approximately 116;000 user records belonging to the Western Australian educational publisher. While the actor alleged exposure of deep personally identifiable information (PII)—including order archives; customer contact lines; and localized payment methods—R.I.C. Publications released an official corporate disclosure clarifying that the security anomaly was restricted entirely to an automated website email relay function with zero systemic infrastructure penetration or client data leakage." Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Commercial solar and clean energy provider database dropped entirely online by actor 2019". The leaked tables featured localized customer grid setup records; residential install notes; phone numbers; and physical addresses." Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: National brick-and-mortar bookstore chain suffered an e-commerce plugin architecture compromise. Threat actor Dumpdump" extracted customer profile parameters; retail transaction histories; and active loyalty club tracking tables." Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: An underground cybercrime forum listing asserted the successful exploitation of an administrative dataset originating from Centrelink's internal Advice of Death" reporting workflow. Threat actor "2019" claims the exposure of over 2;100 highly sensitive records; allegedly encompassing deceased citizen metrics; national healthcare identifiers; social security reference numbers; relationship statuses; and explicit contact PII belonging to executors and next-of-kin." Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: A malicious threat actor operating under the alias 2019" leaked a database containing more than 53;300 customer account records belonging to Sydney-based luxury travel agency FirstClass.com.au on an underground hacking forum. The exfiltrated data was made available for download at no cost and compromised personal details including names; phone numbers; email addresses; IP addresses; account statuses; and preferred flight launch airports. Security reviews of the published samples indicated the bulk of populated records were restricted to core personal contact fields. The threat actor responsible has targeted an estimated 19 Australian organizations in early 2026." Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: McAfee Labs issued threat intelligence warnings regarding an aggressive Malware-as-a-Service campaign named 'WeedHack' targeting Australian gamers. Disguised as free Minecraft mods and performance clients distributed via SEO-poisoned websites and YouTube links; the payload functions as an info-stealer and remote access trojan (RAT) that harvests credentials; crypto-wallets; and enables unauthorized webcam surveillance. Incident type: Malware / Exploit; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: The Australian Centre for the Moving Image fell victim to a SQL database exfiltration. Threat actor 2019" posted a clean user repository containing visitor login credentials; full names; email addresses; and subscription histories." Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Commercial property firm targeted during a wider sector campaign. Threat actor 2019" published an active CRM database slice containing commercial leasing records; property portfolios; and private investor profile metrics." Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Major corporate workplace catering platform hit by actor 2019".
