Threat actors exfiltrated 62.2GB of data; compromising student medical records; confidential non-disclosure agreements; and employee Tax File Numbers (TFNs). The breach caused widespread operational paralysis just weeks before the first semester; crippling enrollment portals; internal communications; and graduation tracking. The university subsequently obtained a Supreme Court injunction against Persons Unknown" to legally prohibit the online dissemination of the stolen data and engaged the ATO to secure impacted TFNs." Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: The Akira ransomware syndicate posted an exfiltrated data archive containing corporate files from a closed Australian media production asset division. Stolen directories included historical distributor agreements and legacy employee payroll records. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Local government municipality confirmed a December network encryption event. The SafePay ransomware group subsequently published 175GB of exfiltrated municipal files on the dark web; containing local council infrastructure development maps; ratepayer billing directories; and staff files. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Muswellbrook Shire Council in New South Wales discovered unauthorised access to its IT environment on 4 December 2024. The SafePay ransomware gang subsequently published 175 gigabytes of stolen council data on 15 December 2024. The council notified relevant authorities including the Australian Cyber Security Centre, NSW Information and Privacy Commissioner, and the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner, and directly contacted affected individuals.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Following its major 2024 cyberattack and subsequent liquidation; a massive cache of stolen MediSecure data was definitively hosted on a public leak site. The dataset contained highly confidential records; including full patient names; contact details; prescription medications; and specific health identifiers linked to national electronic prescription networks. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: Domestic consumer goods manufacturer Natures Organics confirmed a network encryption event by the Medusa ransomware gang. Threat actors published scanned driver's licenses; corporate passports; employee payroll logs; and supply chain shipping contracts as dark web proof. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Hacking collective RipperSec targeted a prominent online Australian rare automotive parts documentation database and marketplace. The incident formed part of a wider ideological hacktivism campaign directed against corporate web assets across Oceania. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Unique Cars and Parts, an Australian website that helps users find specific parts for rare and unique vehicles, was targeted by the RipperSec hacking group in January 2025. The incident was part of a broader campaign by hacktivist groups targeting Australian organisations, with RipperSec collaborating with DXPLOIT under the "OpsAustralia" banner to launch attacks against Australian websites.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Automotive engineering and clutch kit parts manufacturer Clutch Industries suffered an external cyber incident. Internal corporate file servers were accessed via an unpatched VPN edge device; leading to the extraction of localized trade logistics spreadsheets. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Australian automotive manufacturer Clutch Industries confirmed a cyber incident in January 2025 after the Lynx ransomware group listed the company on its darknet leak site. The attackers claimed to have exfiltrated 350 gigabytes of data including business records, employee information, and financial details.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Commercial construction firm Novati Constructions was listed on the Lynx ransomware darknet leak page. Threat actors stated they successfully exfiltrated internal financial audits; building tender documents; legal project contracts; and workplace safety incident logs. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Novati Constructions, a Sydney-based construction firm established in 1971, was listed on the Lynx ransomware gang's dark web leak site on 13 January 2025. The attackers claimed to have stolen business and personal data including contracts, financial records, and incident reports from the company, which specialises in construction, refurbishment, and heritage restoration in the Sydney basin.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: A prominent dark web threat actor falsely claimed to possess an exfiltrated database containing 12;000;000 customer accounts belonging to the consumer electronics retailer. Following a comprehensive internal forensic review; JB Hi-Fi officially denied any underlying network breach. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Ideological hacking group RipperSec executed a targeted web asset compromise directed against a specialized physics research sub-portal hosted by the University of NSW. The incident resulted in web defacement and localized directory access. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: Emerging cybercrime group Morpheus claimed credit for a historical August 2024 network intrusion targeting pharmaceutical distributor DBG Health. To force ransom negotiation; threat actors published scanned employee passports and corporate logistics records on the dark web. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: DBG Health, an Australian pharmaceuticals and healthcare firm that owns the country's largest generic drug manufacturer Arrotex, suffered a ransomware attack in August 2024. The newly emerged Morpheus ransomware gang claimed responsibility in January 2025, posting employee passport scans and confidential business documents to the dark web as proof. DBG Health acknowledged the breach on 25 August 2024, confirming unauthorised access to a storage server.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: The Qilin ransomware syndicate listed international freight forwarding specialist Globelink on its dark web data leak site. Hacking groups asserted they exfiltrated nearly 30;000 files covering customs declarations; shipping manifests; and client billing logs. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Wealth management and financial advisory firm Austin's Financial Solutions fell victim to a Kairos ransomware deployment. Hacking groups exfiltrated and subsequently published a 147GB data vault containing sensitive client investment portfolios and income statements. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Smart parking application CellOPark investigated a database integration anomaly after Brisbane municipal parking app users received highly anomalous; targeted marketing and phishing emails. Cloud notification keys rotated. Incident type: Phishing; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: On 20 December 2024, CellOPark users received confusing messages about their accounts being transitioned to a new platform called OPark, sparking data breach concerns. The situation escalated when users received contradictory emails—first announcing the transition, then instructing users to disregard it, followed by confirmation the transition would proceed. CellOPark assured users no private information was compromised but notified the Information Commissioner as a precaution. The incident stemmed from a commercial dispute with the overseas supplier rather than an external cyber attack.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Industrial tiling; flooring; and waterproofing chemicals manufacturer ARDEX Australia suffered a system-wide encryption event. The Medusa ransomware operation claimed responsibility; establishing a dark web countdown clock threatening the release of corporate data. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: INC Ransom claimed responsibility for a targeted network security incident affecting a private Sydney-based diagnostic medical imaging practice. Forensic teams isolated clinical imaging modalities from administrative scheduling shares to complete mitigation. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: Medium.

records.organisation: Fresh Produce Safety Centre Australia & New Zealand (FPSC)
records.summary: The incident register reports: Cybersecurity researchers identified an unsecured database node associated with WACER and the University of Sydney-based FPSC. The open segment exposed joint research project documentation; internal operational emails; and corporate stakeholder contact indices before being restricted by network administrators. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: The Medusa ransomware group claimed an enterprise-wide intrusion targeting global digital gaming and slot machine manufacturer Ainsworth Game Technology. Threat actors published proof of an 852.4GB exfiltrated dataset detailing technical source codes. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: On 10 December 2024, the Medusa ransomware group listed Ainsworth Game Technology, an Australian manufacturer of gaming machines and software with global operations, on its leak site claiming to have stolen 852.4 gigabytes of data. The attackers demanded $1.2 million USD and set a deadline of 24 December 2024, threatening to release the stolen data if payment was not received. The compromised data included employee passports, tax file numbers, bank account details, and confidential business information from Ainsworth's operations across Australia, New Zealand, Asia, the United States, and Europe.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Applied behavioural science consultancy Evidn; which operates closely alongside the Queensland state government; was listed by the Everest ransomware gang. Threat actors claimed the theft of 50GB of files containing policy research telemetry. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: Private digital educational tutoring support platform TFTH fell victim to a network breach claimed by the KillSec ransomware syndicate. Threat actors targeted student portal directories to access customer subscription logs and payment profiles. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: In December 2024, the KillSec ransomware gang claimed an attack on Thanks for the Help (TFTH), an Australian educational support platform that assists university and college students with assessments and student accommodation services. KillSec threatened to leak exfiltrated data after eight days and published 1% of allegedly stolen data as proof. TFTH's website has been flagged by the Australian government's Tertiary Education Quality and Standards Agency for providing essay writing services.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: A malicious cyber syndicate targeted the legacy IT infrastructure of Queensland-based firm Nicholsons Solicitors. Hacking groups discovered unprotected document repositories containing client transactional history sheets left active following operational closure. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: On 24 November 2024, the INC Ransom gang claimed responsibility for hacking Nicholsons Solicitors, a now-closed Brisbane law firm, exposing at least 250 gigabytes of client data including correspondence, court documents, bank account details, and property deeds. The breach occurred after the firm closed without naming a successor practice, leaving legacy data unprotected on servers with no clear custodian. The Queensland Law Society confirmed no successor practice was appointed, highlighting significant cybersecurity risks when businesses shut down without proper data management arrangements.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: The Hellcat extortion group breached Schneider Electric's internal project tracking software (Jira). The threat actors exfiltrated 40 gigabytes of data; including sensitive corporate infrastructure plans; engineering project logs; and internal developer communications. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Schneider Electric allegedly suffered a second cyber attack in 2024 when the Hellcat ransomware group claimed responsibility for breaching the company's Atlassian Jira system. A threat actor named "greppy" posted sample stolen data to X (formerly Twitter) on November 4, 2024.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Cisco investigated a data leak after threat actors posted proprietary corporate developer metrics on an underground forum. The stolen files included internal GitHub developer logs; API configuration schemas; and private cloud storage buckets exposed via a compromised contractor account. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Clinical support provider Equinox formally disclosed a network data breach. Security analysts confirmed that an unauthorized third party bypassed access barriers to look at localized data volumes detailing clinical patient registration profiles and internal staff logs. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: The Australian division of the major Japanese dairy manufacturer confirmed a targeted network intrusion. IT security teams executed isolation protocols; limiting data compromise to a distinct subset of historical corporate employee records. OAIC updated. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Snow Brand Australia, the Australian arm of Japanese dairy company Snow Brand, confirmed it was the victim of a SafePay ransomware attack in November 2024. The breach resulted in exposure of a 24-gigabyte dataset containing financial documents, business records, and sensitive employee information.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Australian mortgage brokerage aggregator Finsure confirmed a corporate cyber incident after nearly 300;000 unique corporate email addresses; broker correspondence strings; and profile logs appeared on the data breach indexing site Have I Been Pwned. Incident type: Phishing; source-rated severity: High. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: On 15 October 2024, Australian mortgage broking group Finsure experienced a data breach affecting 296,124 customers and brokers when compromised credentials allowed unauthorized access to marketing data on third-party platform ActivePipe. The breach was publicly disclosed on 19 November 2024 through Have I Been Pwned. Compromised data included names, phone numbers, physical addresses, and email addresses, though Finsure confirmed no passwords or financial data were exposed. The incident did not directly affect Finsure's systems. Finsure confirmed the cyber incident and stated there was no evidence of misuse or publication of individual personal information. The company worked with ActivePipe to remediate the credential compromise and reset access controls.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: The RansomHub syndicate claimed an enterprise network breach targeting Waive;" a critical third-party compliance platform integrated with the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC). Forensic reviews were launched into corporate client document vaults." Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: The prominent threat actor IntelBroker successfully exfiltrated a significant cache of internal files from a third-party developer portal used by Nokia. The leaked material included proprietary source code components; ssh keys; security certificates; and corporate project blueprints. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Amazon confirmed a data exposure affecting internal employee directories. A threat actor exploited a vulnerability in a third-party property management system to exfiltrate corporate contact information; including employee work email addresses; desk phone numbers; and building locations. No customer or financial data was compromised. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

records.organisation: Coroners Court of Victoria / Tasmanian Chamber of Commerce
records.summary: The incident register reports: Infamous threat syndicate NoName launched a series of coordinated infrastructure attacks targeting nine separate Australian public sector web assets. The Victorian Coroners Court and the Tasmanian Chamber of Commerce confirmed localized web asset containment. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: Wollongong-based corporate office supplier confirmed an operational ransomware attack. Local IT networks were isolated to prevent lateral movement; and emergency manual ordering procedures were briefly deployed across physical warehouse locations. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Micon Office National, a Wollongong-based office furniture supplier, was attacked by the Sarcoma ransomware gang on November 3, 2024. The attack resulted in a three-day business shutdown while IT systems were restored, with the company choosing not to pay the ransom.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: A malicious dark web threat actor listed a stolen database archive for sale containing the text records; employee identification profiles; and internal corporate email listings of over 44;000 historical and active Telstra staff members. Core telecommunications assets safe. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Telstra suffered a data breach affecting approximately 44,000 employees and partners when threat actor "UnicornLover67" gained unauthorised access to a pre-production test environment using stolen credentials. The breach exposed employee contact information but did not compromise customer data, passwords or financial information.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: NSW-based community health and social support provider suffered a perimeter security breach. External forensic analysts confirmed unauthorized access to an internal database; exposing sensitive patient clinical care records; contact logs; and history sheets. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Commercial project management and consulting arm of the Australian National University; ANU Enterprise (ANUE); confirmed a ransomware attack. Institutional backups were deployed to recover administrative configurations. The core university mainframe remained isolated. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Aged care provider suffered a major data exfiltration event. Threat actors claimed to have exfiltrated massive terabyte-scale data volumes from corporate storage directories; including resident identity logs and elder care clinical documents. OAIC notified. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: The NSW Privacy Commissioner issued formal operational advisories to WSU as the ongoing forensic review into their multi-stage 2024 breach revealed deeply rooted adversarial mapping. Security teams executed a final wholesale tier-reset of legacy network access permissions. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: A severe configuration glitch during a routine commercial app update allowed frequent flyer members to view the boarding passes; flight details; and booking metrics of entirely random; unrelated passengers within their own mobile app interfaces. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Qantas discovered that employees of its ground handling partner India SATS had exploited their booking system access to steal frequent flyer points and alter customer bookings, potentially accessing passport details of over 800 customers. The fraudulent activity occurred between July and August 2024 and involved employees changing customer frequent flyer account details to redirect earned points to accounts they controlled.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Major Australian corporate entities were swept into a global supply chain incident targeting US networking giant Cisco. Threat actors scraped partner portal records; briefly leaking metadata strings linked to Australian enterprise accounts. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Security researchers flagged a brief public exposure involving a cloud-hosted development directory managed by Deloitte. The isolated segment contained internal testing keys; software build configurations; and non-production metadata before it was permanently secured. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Catastrophic database compromise saw the exfiltration of 31;000;000 unique international user accounts; including a massive Australian consumer subset. Compromised data included email addresses; internal usernames; and bcrypt-hashed passwords. Coordinated with a simultaneous DDoS attack. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: On 9 October 2024, the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine breach was dramatically announced via JavaScript alert: "Have you ever felt like the Internet Archive runs on sticks and is constantly on the verge of suffering a catastrophic security breach? It just happened. See 31 million of you on HIBP!" The attacker stole a 6.4GB database on 28 September containing 31 million users' email addresses, screen names, password change timestamps, and Bcrypt-hashed passwords. The breach coincided with BlackMeta DDoS attacks (believed unconnected). On 20 October, a second breach compromised the Zendesk support email system.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Indonesian government digital immigration portal suffered a critical database indexing configuration glitch. The system failure temporarily exposed the high-resolution passport scans and flight detail logs of thousands of Australian tourists traveling to Bali. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Indonesia's e-visa system experienced a glitch in October 2024 that inadvertently exposed passport details of travelers including Australians visiting Bali. At least three separate Australian travelers reported being able to view full names, dates of birth, passport numbers, and photos of strangers when scanning QR codes on their visa documents.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Global financial transfer giant suffered a severe infrastructure outage followed by a verified data breach that disrupted services for its extensive Australian user base. Exfiltrated fields included customer identity documents and historical transaction logs. Incident type: DDoS; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Parent operating entity of Strike Bowling; Holy Moley; and associated entertainment venues confirmed a network-wide cyber incident. Forensic analysis identified a ransom payload targeting corporate point-of-sale servers. High-level containment was executed. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Dell notified internal corporate teams of a third-party partner platform compromise. An unauthorized actor breached an external contractor's data environment; exfiltrating limited operational setups; corporate procurement orders; and basic internal service tags. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Dell Technologies experienced two alleged data breaches within one weekend in September 2024, affecting over 10,800 employees. The first breach on 19 September exposed employee IDs, names, and employment status. A second breach was claimed on 22 September involving compromised Atlassian tools (Jira, Jenkins, Confluence) containing 3.5GB of internal data. Dell confirmed they were investigating the claims.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Confirmed 18 Sep 2024. 440GB of sensitive corporate engineering data was exposed on a public file-sharing platform after an extortionist named Fortibitch" bypassed access tokens on a third-party cloud storage bucket. Australian enterprise deployment paths were audited." Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Fortinet, a global cybersecurity company, confirmed a data breach in September 2024 after a threat actor claimed to have stolen 440GB of customer data from the company's Azure SharePoint instance. Fortinet refused to pay the ransom demand, and the attacker subsequently leaked the data. The breach affected less than 0.3% of Fortinet customers, primarily in the APAC region, potentially including Australian customers.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: A threat actor attempted to sell an alleged database containing millions of user profiles on a hacking forum. While Temu strongly denied any backend system breach; independent security analysts cross-verified that small subsets of the leaked formatting matched active public-facing account schemas. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: National audiology and hearing clinic network suffered a customer database breach. An unauthorized third party targeted a misconfigured cloud repository to scrape the health treatment schedules; names; and contact details of tens of thousands of patients. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Australia's largest private diagnostic imaging network launched an emergency remediation campaign after discovering that a legacy patient web login portal had left tens of thousands of diagnostic radiology files and profile records exposed online for nearly a year. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Australia's largest medical imaging provider I-MED Radiology suffered a data breach when login credentials for three healthcare professional accounts were compromised and used to access tens of thousands of patient records. The credentials had been publicly available online for an extended period before the breach was discovered in September 2024, allowing unauthorized access to patient information dating back to 2006. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: In September 2024, I-MED Radiology Network, Australia's largest medical imaging provider, exposed tens of thousands of patient files online for over a year through a misconfigured online referrer portal. Patient medical imaging records and personal information were accessible using details that had been shared publicly online.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Major consumer electronics and camera retail chain fell victim to an external database intrusion. A malicious threat actor listed an exfiltrated SQL file tree for sale on a dark web marketplace containing retail customer registration fields and e-commerce transactions. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Australian consumer electronics retailer digiDirect suffered a data breach affecting 304,337 customers when a threat actor using the alias "Tanaka" exfiltrated customer database records and posted them on dark web forums. The breach, discovered on September 29, 2024, exposed personal information and partial payment card details. DigiDirect Group owns digiDirect, Booktopia, Angus & Robertson, and computer hardware retailer Mwave.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Nationwide trade tool retail franchise chain Total Tools confirmed a localized customer data leak. Threat actors targeted a web-facing loyalty program server to exfiltrate trade member contact logs; phone numbers; and promotional logs for thousands of tool rewards cardholders. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: In September 2024, Australian hardware retailer Total Tools suffered a data breach exposing personal details of approximately 38,000 customers including names, email addresses, phone numbers, and physical addresses through a cyber attack.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Cloud-based allied health practice management software provider Power Diary suffered an authorized session token bypass. Threat actors used the compromised developer panel to blast malicious medical phishing and spam emails directly to patients. Incident type: Phishing; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Non-profit fundraising; charitable gaming; and donation management aggregate BSG Australia was listed as a victim by the RansomHub group. Internal forensic teams immediately isolated cloud donor tracking directories to evaluate exfiltration depth. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: BSG Australia, a supplier of bingo and fundraising supplies for clubs and hospitality venues, was listed on the RansomHub ransomware gang's darknet leak site on 9 September 2024. The attackers claimed to have exfiltrated 79 gigabytes of data and set a ransom deadline of 24 September. RansomHub shared three stolen documents as proof of the breach.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Global vehicle rental provider Avis confirmed a cloud infrastructure security incident that impacted a subset of Australian consumers. Threat actors gained unauthorized entry to a corporate file directory containing historic vehicle rental customer contracts. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Specialist motorcycle and specialty vehicle underwriting agency Protecta Australia investigated an active network incident after a dark web forum administrator posted a stolen database file containing client vehicle policy registration entries for sale. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Protecta Australia, a flooring and service protection provider, had a customer database containing information for 74,373 customers listed for sale on BreachForums on 6 September 2024. A threat actor using the name "agreindex" claimed to have exfiltrated the database in September 2024 and offered it for sale on the dark web.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Outdoor outfitter and commercial equipment manufacturer White Mountain Backpacks was listed on the Rhysida ransomware syndicate's darknet platform. Leaked files included domestic warehouse distribution lists and commercial retail accounting files. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: White Mountain Backpacks, an Australian outfitter specializing in custom fitted travel backpacks, was listed by the Rhysida ransomware gang on 1 September 2024. The attackers posted images of approximately 20 documents as proof of the breach, including trust account statements, receipts, signed documents, and spreadsheets. Rhysida set a ransom deadline of 7 September.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Swinburne University of Technology confirmed that the shared network architecture supporting its international Sarawak Campus was targeted by an advanced persistent threat (APT) actor. Student enrollment matrices and staff identity logs were accessed. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: National medical charity Australian Cancer Research Foundation (ACRF) issued formal notifications to its donor base detailing a data security incident. An unauthorized entity bypassed entry boundaries on a historical donor profile storage drive. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Family location tracking and safety application Life360 suffered an extensive data breach that exposed 442;000 global customer records. Malicious actors exploited a vulnerable cloud developer API to scrape account usernames; emails; and phone markers. Significant AU impact. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: ASX-listed gold mining enterprise Evolution Mining officially disclosed a network cyber incident. While automated subterranean mining machinery and regional refinement operations remained safe; a forensic investigation was launched into administrative file share access. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Evolution Mining, one of Australia's largest gold producers, became aware of a ransomware attack on 8 August 2024 that impacted its IT systems. The investigation determined the data breach primarily relates to Evolution's Northparkes Operations and files stored on Northparkes servers. The company engaged external cybersecurity experts and confirmed the attack was fully contained with no material impact anticipated on operations.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Large Victorian regional community support and child development not-for-profit entity Meli confirmed a perimeter network security incident. IT monitoring systems blocked cross-network expansion; safeguarding primary social care case logs. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Meli, a North Geelong-based community support service, was hit by a Qilin ransomware attack on 21 August 2024. The attackers stole 215 gigabytes of data (419,617 files), including financial statements, confidentiality agreements, passport scans, and Medicare cards. The organization operates over 30 kindergartens and provides family support and foster care services in the Geelong region.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Queensland-headquartered diving equipment supplier Adreno—widely cited as one of the world's largest dive retail platforms—investigated dark web cyber claims after a malicious actor offered a scraped e-commerce customer listing file for sale. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Adreno, an Australian dive store claiming to operate the world's largest dive store on the Gold Coast, suffered a data breach affecting more than 500,000 customers. The breach was discovered on 12 August 2024 when the Australian Cyber Security Centre notified the company about a breach affecting their point-of-sale (POS) software. Customer names, addresses, phone numbers, and email addresses were exposed.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Global flight tracking and aviation telemetry service FlightAware issued a data security warning to its international user base; including a substantial Australian pilot and aviation enthusiast subset; following a configuration change that left profile settings exposed. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Regional civil engineering and infrastructure component manufacturer Hudson Civil Engineering was targeted by the RansomHub syndicate. Threat actors published corporate payroll sheets; project construction quotes; and council supply tenders. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Hudson Civil Engineering, a Launceston-based Tasmanian engineering firm, was targeted by the RansomHub ransomware gang in August 2024. The attackers claimed to have stolen 112 gigabytes of data and threatened to release it on their darknet leak site. The attack was announced on 7 August 2024 as part of a broader campaign by RansomHub targeting Australian engineering firms.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Heavy industrial engineering and hydraulic systems specialist Kempe Engineering was listed on the RansomHub darknet leak site following an unpatched VPN edge device breach. Leaked materials were restricted to historical logistics files. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Kempe Engineering, a Geelong-based specialist engineering firm, was targeted by the RansomHub ransomware gang in a major attack that resulted in the theft of approximately 4 terabytes of data. records.summary: The incident register reports: Nationwide home furniture and lifestyle retail chain Early Settler officially confirmed a customer data breach. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: On 3 August 2024, threat actor "Worry" posted Early Settler customer data for sale on a hacking forum for USD $2,000, exposing 1.1 million customers' names, email addresses, phone numbers, delivery addresses, and some dates of birth from an archived database dating to July 2022. Payment information was not compromised as Early Settler does not hold credit/bank card details. The company notified affected customers, OAIC, ACSC, and New Zealand authorities.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: McDowall Affleck, a Perth-based engineering firm, confirmed it was hit by a RansomHub ransomware attack that resulted in the theft of nearly 500 gigabytes of data. The attack occurred on 24 July 2024, with the company's network encrypted and confidential data exfiltrated. RansomHub publicly announced the attack on 1 August 2024.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Following up on their May incident; WSU discovered that the persistent adversary had accessed a broader range of historical storage drives. records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: A malicious actor leaked a database list from a 2022 Roblox developer conference. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Roblox announced on 24 July 2024 that attendees of the 2022, 2023, and 2024 Roblox Developer Conference were impacted by a data breach at FNTech, the third-party vendor handling conference registrations. The breach exposed names, email addresses, and IP addresses of 10,386 conference attendees after someone gained unauthorized access to FNTech's systems. The breach was first reported by Have I Been Pwned on 4 July 2024.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: South Australian regional municipality Wattle Range Council confirmed a severe network security breach after being listed by the LockBit ransomware syndicate. Council engineers isolated local administrative networks and deployed off-site clean backups for recovery. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Wattle Range Council in South Australia was targeted by the LockBit ransomware gang in July 2024. The attackers stole 103 gigabytes of data across more than 46,000 files and threatened to publish the information on 4 August unless an unspecified ransom was paid. The NSW Supreme Court granted an injunction on 2 August to restrain third parties from accessing or disseminating the breached data.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Major Australian medical education and professional development platform Healthed experienced a perimeter data breach. Security sweeps identified unauthorized SQL command executions that briefly exposed general practitioner contact directories. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Healthed, Australia's largest provider of continuing professional development (CPD) for general practitioners, discovered a website vulnerability on July 14, 2024 caused by work undertaken by a third-party contractor. The vulnerability exposed contact details of between 500 to 1,000 GPs who had attended Healthed's face-to-face educational seminars. The company resolved the issue within two hours of discovery and confirmed no credit card information was compromised.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Supply chain cyber security incident affecting the City of Ballarat via a data breach at its contracted after-hours customer call center provider; OracleCMS. Municipal ratepayer service call logs and contact numbers were briefly leaked online. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: National multi-disciplinary allied health and physical rehabilitation network confirmed an administrative network data breach. External forensic teams were deployed to trace potential exposure vectors across regional patient therapy databases. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: The remote connectivity software provider detected an unauthorized intrusion into its internal corporate IT environment. The attack; attributed to Russian state-sponsored actors; was contained to the corporate network and did not impact the production environment or customer software infrastructure. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Massive international fintech banking provider Evolve Bank & Trust suffered a severe database compromise that trickled down to impact Australian consumers utilizing the Wise money transfer platform. Exfiltrated items included international transaction logs. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: City of Yarra municipal council in inner Melbourne suffered a double data breach after an internal technical parsing error accidentally listed ratepayer identity fields and municipal planning submission files on a publicly indexable web directory. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Global retail apparel giant Levi Strauss suffered a credential stuffing campaign that compromised 72;000 user accounts worldwide; including a localized Australian customer segment. Malicious actors accessed saved retail profile metrics and purchase track lists. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Popular Australian order-ahead hospitality and coffee application Hey You fell victim to an external database breach. A malicious threat actor exfiltrated a user repository containing the phone numbers; names; and hashed login data of over 100;000 users. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Australian food ordering service Hey You was allegedly breached by a threat actor using the alias "Billy100," who claimed to have stolen data from over 100,000 customers and partners. The attacker posted 202,488 lines of data for sale on BreachForums on June 25, 2024, comprising two separate datasets with customer information and credentials. As of the initial disclosure, there was no evidence that Hey You had formally notified the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner or that affected customers received direct notification. The lack of official confirmation and formal notification raised concerns about transparency and compliance with Australia's Notifiable Data Breaches scheme.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: A business email compromise (BEC) campaign directed against an external corporate supplier of the Victorian Auditor-General’s Office (VAGO) resulted in the unauthorized alteration of banking routing records and the diversion of state administrative funds. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: A June 2024 audit by the Victorian Auditor-General's Office revealed that cyber criminals had accessed Victorian government departments' vendor master file on four occasions over an 18-month period, altering supplier bank account details to redirect payments to fraudulent accounts.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Queensland regional municipal council launched an active forensic investigation after discovering that a misconfigured third-party data visualization plugin had leaked local ratepayer mapping entries and property contact numbers online. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: City of Moreton Bay Council in Queensland experienced an accidental data exposure in June 2024 when private ratepayer information was published on the council's website. The breach occurred through the council's customer inquiries portal, exposing personal details and complaint records.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Prominent Australian food manufacturer Patties Foods—producers of Four'N Twenty pies—experienced an administrative data leak. Security analysts tracked the incident to an unencrypted development server file share containing logistics timelines. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: In June 2024, researcher Jeremiah Fowler discovered non-password-protected databases belonging to Patties Foods (Four'N Twenty, Leggo's, Nanna's) managed by third-party Provenio.ai. The exposure included 524k documents: a logging server with 496,296 records plus 25,800 invoices/distribution records containing vendor contacts, emails, banking account numbers, invoice amounts, supplier information, and employee names. Provenio restricted access within hours of notification. Patties claimed "technically wasn't a breach" but a "data exposure" with no evidence of malicious access. Vendor and employee contact information and banking details were exposed but no evidence of malicious access was found.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Large-scale Victorian regional transport and freight carrier company suffered a major network intrusion. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Victorian Freight Specialists, a logistics company serving regional Victoria and southern NSW, was breached by hacking group GhostR on May 26, 2024, with the attack publicly disclosed on June 4. The attackers claimed to have stolen over 846 gigabytes of data from the company's server networks.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: The ShinyHunters syndicate claimed the massive exfiltration of 500;000;000 global customer records from a corporate Snowflake cloud storage container. Stolen data totaled 1.3TB and included customer names; encrypted payment tracking metrics; and historical ticketing records. Massive AU volume. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: WSU disclosed a significant network breach where unauthorized actors gained access to its Microsoft 365 cloud environment. The intruders intercepted internal communications and accessed student and staff corporate email accounts; forcing a widespread security lockdown. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Computer manufacturing multinational Dell issued an emergency notification to 49;000;000 global customers; including an extensive Australian consumer segment. A threat actor named Menelik" systematically scraped full client names; physical shipping addresses; and hardware purchasing logs via a vulnerable; partner-facing API portal." Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Petrochemical multinational Shell investigated a supply chain database extraction event after malicious threat actors offered a stolen customer dataset containing localized Australian retail fuel card account profiles for sale on an illicit forum. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: In May 2024, Shell disclosed a data breach affecting approximately 80,000 customers across multiple countries, including Australians shopping at Shell Coles Express locations. The breach occurred through a third-party mystery shopping vendor that experienced a cybersecurity incident. Compromised data included customer names, email addresses, mobile phone numbers, postcodes, and internal customer identifiers ("shopper codes"). Shell emphasized that the breach originated from the vendor's systems rather than Shell's own infrastructure, though the data related to Shell customer loyalty programs. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Shell suffered a data breach in May 2024 affecting its customer loyalty program in multiple countries including Australia. A threat actor known as "888" posted 80,000 rows of customer data to BreachForums, with sample data showing Australian customers shopping at Shell Coles Express locations.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Commercial printing and corporate publishing specialist Advance Press suffered a perimeter breach. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Advance Press, a Western Australia-based printing organization, was breached by the Ransom House threat group in May 2024. records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Concentrated supply chain cyber incident affecting Nissan Australia and New Zealand operations. records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

The incident register reports: Retail energy; electricity; and broadband provider Sumo officially confirmed a serious customer data breach. Malicious actors accessed central account directories; exposing consumer electricity billing details and connection histories. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Sumo, an Australian energy and internet provider, suffered a data breach when customer information was accessed via an unsecured Amazon S3 bucket. records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Major Victorian public healthcare network Monash Health was swept into a supply chain ransomware breach targeting ZircoDATA; its contracted historical document archiving vendor. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: More than one million Australian ID records were exposed in a data breach affecting patrons of pubs and clubs across NSW, ACT, and Victoria in May 2024. records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Islamic co-educational college in Victoria investigated a localized cyber security incident. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: A database containing information for approximately 750 students from Victoria's Mt Hira College was circulated on a popular hacking forum on 27 April 2024. The database includes student names, student IDs, classes, email addresses, and passwords in plain text. The data was offered for free on the forum and appears to use very common word and number combinations for passwords.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: State emergency medical provider Ambulance Victoria discovered a data leak window after an internal technical shift left an administrative roster folder unsecured. The mobile contact numbers of active on-duty paramedic crews were briefly visible online. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Ambulance Victoria exposed staff members' personal mobile phone numbers and rostering status through a misconfigured intranet page accessible to the entire workforce in April 2024. The Victorian Ambulance Union was notified of the breach and demanded complete removal of mobile numbers, staff notification, and an audit of access duration. This incident marked the third privacy breach at Ambulance Victoria within a year, raising serious concerns about the organization's data protection practices.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Nationwide provider of residential smoke alarm compliance services Smoke Alarm Solutions suffered a perimeter security breach. Homeowners and real estate property managers were urged to watch for targeted phishing scams following customer profile exfiltration. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Smoke Alarm Solutions, Australia's largest smoke alarm installation and service provider, left a database containing 762,856 documents (107GB) publicly accessible without password protection. Discovered by cybersecurity researcher Jeremiah Fowler in April 2024, the exposure included detailed customer invoices, property addresses, and service records spanning 2021-2024. Despite multiple disclosure attempts over nearly two months, the company's legal representatives claimed the incident did not constitute a notifiable data breach under Australian law.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Global consumer drone and aerial camera manufacturing giant DJI was targeted by the ideologically motivated cyber collective R00TK1T. The threat actors published internal code configurations and local dealer communications logs covering Oceania operations. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: The digital ticketing and customer pre-registration database supporting the Pandemonium Rocks music festival suffered an external intrusion; exposing music fan contact entries and ticket confirmation codes. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Pandemonium Rocks music festival exposed personal and banking information of over 400 ticketholders on April 19, 2024 when an admin tab was accidentally left enabled on a refund request form. The breach occurred during a tumultuous period for the festival after 7 of 13 scheduled bands canceled, prompting attendees to request partial refunds. The exposed data—visible for just 7 minutes between 7:13pm and 7:20pm—included names, bank account details (BSB and account numbers), email addresses, and phone numbers.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: High-severity data leak targeting Telstra's Opticomm fiber infrastructure network. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: Commercial logistics and express freight network BHF Couriers launched a forensic audit following dark web allegations of financial database theft. The company issued a statement denying claims that active consumer credit card hashes were compromised. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Global digital streaming hardware provider Roku suffered a major secondary credential stuffing breach that compromised 576;000 user accounts worldwide; including a substantial Australian consumer footprint. Attackers attempted fraudulent subscription modifications. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Suncorp Bank investigated a targeted cyber fraud event. A technical parameter flaw in a digital banking web portal allowed unauthorized entities to intercept transaction validations; resulting in the localized theft of consumer funds before deployment of a security patch. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Suncorp Bank, part of major Australian insurance and banking conglomerate Suncorp Group, experienced a cyber attack in April 2024 where unauthorized third parties gained access to a small number of customer accounts and stole funds. The bank successfully recovered and returned all stolen funds to affected customers—a rare outcome in digital breach cases. Suncorp restricted affected accounts, reset passwords, and activated fraud prevention protocols.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Western Australian public health support body Diabetes WA officially disclosed a network data breach. Threat actors bypassed edge security controls on a legacy participant database; exposing health-related membership contact indices. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Diabetes WA, a Western Australian healthcare organization providing services for people with diabetes, disclosed a data breach on April 2, 2024 affecting users of its telehealth service. The breach occurred when a single compromised user account was exploited by a third party, providing access to personal information including Medicare numbers, health details, and contact information. The organization quickly detected and contained the breach, blocking the compromised account and notifying all affected individuals. The organization emphasized that the breach was quickly detected and fully contained, with no evidence of ongoing unauthorized access after the compromised account was blocked. However, the incident highlighted the risks of credential-based attacks on healthcare organizations, where a single compromised account can provide access to sensitive patient information.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Australia's largest motorcycle dealership operator; Motorcycle Holdings; experienced a coordinated web asset compromise. Threat actors deployed web shell exploits across several brand-specific retail websites to harvest customer inquiry logs. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: ASX-listed MotorCycle Holdings Limited (MTO) disclosed on April 8, 2024 that a threat actor gained unauthorized access to web servers hosted by a third-party vendor for two of its MOJO Motorcycles brand websites—Sherco and Lambretta. The attacker inserted malicious code that may have exposed customer contact information submitted through web forms. The company's internal systems remained secure and unaffected, with the investigation concluded by April 29, 2024. The company emphasized that its internal systems remained secure throughout the incident, with no evidence of compromise to corporate networks, financial systems, or other operational platforms. This containment to the third-party vendor's infrastructure limited the potential damage and enabled relatively swift resolution.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Recurrent financial system fraud attempt targeting the automated clearing network of the ACT recycling container scheme. Threat actors attempted unauthorized funds redirection via administrative session hijacking; echoing an identical configuration attack from January 2023. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Fujitsu confirmed that multiple corporate computers were infected with advanced malware. An internal investigation revealed that files containing sensitive customer and employee information were exfiltrated from the compromised systems; triggering customer notification protocols. Incident type: Malware / Exploit; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: The global financial institution detected a targeted cyber intrusion that compromised 11 internal IMF email accounts. Security teams isolated the impacted mailboxes to prevent deeper lateral movement across the broader institutional network. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Global merchant and card provider American Express issued formal regulatory notices to Australian credit card holders. The breach originated at an outsourced third-party service provider where a cloud repository containing merchant transaction logs was left exposed. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

records.summary: The incident register reports: The Royal Australian College of General Practitioners (RACGP) suffered a localized server intrusion. Malicious entities bypassed access panels on an administrative database; exfiltrating member general practitioners' mobile numbers; emails; and educational qualification data. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Continuous remediation tracking following a major December 2023 Akira ransomware attack. Nissan Oceania and Nissan Financial Services formally began contacting 100;000 affected Australian and New Zealand customers after validating the exfiltration of government IDs; medical cards; and employment logs. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Non-profit disability employment; training; and workplace placement organization Nova Employment suffered a network data leak. External forensic teams worked to evaluate the exposure of administrative program participant registration files. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Nova Employment, a non-profit organization that provides training, support, and job placements to individuals with disabilities, was targeted by the BlackBasta ransomware gang in March 2024. The organization is part of a broader campaign by BlackBasta targeting multiple Australian organizations during this period.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Global retail footwear brand Vans issued an explicit scam advisory to its international consumer base; including its Australian digital e-commerce subset; following an uncontained network data breach executed by the ALPHV syndicate. The incident register reports: Global fast-food giant McDonald's suffered a massive; simultaneous infrastructure outage that took down physical register screens and mobile ordering apps across Australia. The corporate division issued an official statement denying that a malicious cyber attack caused the network failure. Incident type: DDoS; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Major domestic retail point-of-sale software and infrastructure vendor GaP Solutions confirmed an enterprise network compromise. The incident was claimed by the LockBit syndicate shortly after their global infrastructure reconstruction. Emergency isolation prevented downstream retailer distribution. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: GaP Solutions, an Australian retail software vendor and hardware provider, fell victim to the LockBit ransomware gang in late February/early March 2024. LockBit posted details on its darknet leak site on 29 February, threatening to publish exfiltrated data within 20 days. The attack occurred shortly after international law enforcement disruption of LockBit's operations, demonstrating the gang's quick recovery and continued activity.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Commercial enterprise hosting provider HVD.HOST suffered a hypervisor-level breach. The Black Basta ransomware operation targeted the hosting core; causing simultaneous outages and data extortion events across nearly a dozen downstream Australian small-and-medium businesses. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: The Black Basta ransomware gang compromised a cloud-based hosting service identified only as "hvd.host" in March 2024, affecting approximately 13 Australian companies. The gang posted dozens of Australian passports and driver's licenses to the dark web and threatened to publish data from affected businesses if ransom demands were not met by 9 March 2024. This supply chain attack exposed highly sensitive identity documents from multiple organizations using the hosting service.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: The Mogilevich extortion cartel claimed to have exfiltrated nearly 200 gigabytes of internal product data; email logs; and structural configuration codes from Epic Games' corporate systems. The group used this initial footprint to compromise senior leadership mailboxes; extracting proprietary corporate communications and system defense notes. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The exfiltrated dataset exposed the profile cards of 232;000 active and former subscribers; listing full names; DOBs; emails; and home addresses. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Tangerine Telecom, a popular Australian telecommunications provider owned by Commonwealth Bank, experienced a data breach affecting approximately 232,000 current and former customers. The breach occurred when a third-party contractor's credentials were compromised, allowing unauthorized access to a legacy database containing customer information dating from June 2019 to July 2023.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: The peak national sporting body left an AWS cloud storage directory completely unauthenticated and publicly accessible. The misconfiguration exposed sensitive player registration records; team contracts; and digital passport scans before remediation. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Football Australia, the governing body for soccer in Australia, exposed sensitive personal information of approximately 1,600 A-League players, team personnel, ticket buyers, and family members for 681 days due to AWS access keys hardcoded into a webpage's HTML. Discovered by Cybernews researchers in early February 2024, the misconfiguration allowed public access to 127 Amazon Web Services data buckets containing passport details, player contracts, and personal documents spanning April 2022 to February 2024.

records.summary: The incident register reports: A suspected nation-state adversary infiltrated Cloudflare's self-hosted Atlassian server architecture. Using access credentials compromised during a previous third-party Okta systems breach; the attackers reconnaissance-tested documentation portals and source code repositories before being detected. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Security researchers uncovered a massive; unstructured central storage cluster labeled the Mother of All Breaches" (MOAB). The 12-terabyte archive combined historical leaks with thousands of new data points; exposing user credentials across LinkedIn; Adobe; Twitter; and other corporate architectures." Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: Regional ACT clinical facility Canberra Medical Centre suffered a localized server hack. Malicious threat actors accessed a localized medical records drive; compromising patient clinical intake files and basic contact parameters. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Sydney-based diagnostic imaging operator Quantum Radiology suffered an internal network data breach. Internal communications leaked revealing that administrative management instructed frontline employees to attribute the ensuing system outages to a generic technical fault. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Quantum Radiology, an imaging and diagnostics provider operating 10 clinics across Sydney, fell victim to a ransomware attack on 22 November 2023 that encrypted patient data including medical images, reports, and government health identifiers. The incident was initially attributed to a configuration error but was later revealed as a targeted ransomware attack.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Mid-incident corporate advisory published by Nissan Corporation and Nissan Financial Services Australia/NZ during the initial tracking phases of their Akira ransomware event. Outline detailed active integration with the ACSC to isolate active dealer networks. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Nissan Australia and New Zealand experienced a cyberattack on 5 December 2023 (publicly disclosed in January 2024) when the Akira ransomware group gained unauthorized access to local IT servers. The breach affected approximately 100,000 individuals, including customers of Nissan, Mitsubishi, Renault, Infiniti, and other brands financed through Nissan Financial Services.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive
