records.summary: The incident register reports: A wave of automated credential stuffing campaigns targeted prominent Australian retail; hospitality; and media streaming platforms. Malicious groups utilized credentials stolen from historical global breaches to access saved financial profiles. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: High-profile public sector security breach involving an outsourced file-sharing system used by the Australian Labor Party. The automated extraction resulted in the theft of millions of historical administrative files across multiple overlapping government operational departments. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: Major digital fashion retail platform managed an intense wave of fraudulent account takeovers. Threat actors bypassed customer dashboards using credential stuffing tools; changing account parameters and making unauthorized purchases before the platform initiated merchant chargebacks. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: The Iconic, a popular Australian and New Zealand online fashion retailer with over 2.1 million active customers, experienced an increase in credential stuffing attacks in January 2024. Attackers used stolen login credentials from previous data breaches at other companies to access customer accounts and make fraudulent purchases worth over $1,000 in some cases.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Victorian-headquartered travel agency Inspiring Vacations suffered a severe exposure event when an internal cloud-hosted database holding passenger booking details; itinerary tracking cards; and partial passport parameters was left completely unprotected. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Melbourne-based travel agency Inspiring Vacations exposed the personal information of 112,605 customers through a publicly accessible Amazon Web Services (AWS) S3 storage bucket. The breach, discovered by cybersecurity researcher Jeremiah Fowler in late November 2023, exposed 26.8GB of highly sensitive travel documents including high-resolution passport images, travel visa certificates, and partial credit card numbers.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Critical infrastructure cyber attack targeting Court Services Victoria. The Qilin ransomware syndicate breached the central audiovisual and storage systems; potentially recording or exposing sensitive; sealed court hearings across Supreme; County; and Magistrates courts. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: The Australian and New Zealand division of probiotic beverage manufacturer Yakult confirmed a network breach after threat group DragonForce listed them. The exfiltrated dataset included corporate business records; shipping logs; and employee identity listings. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Global genetic ancestry service 23andMe updated its breach metrics; confirming that threat actors targeted specialized consumer profiles. A significant sub-segment of Australian users had their ancestry profiles and health mapping metadata scraped via credential stuffing. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: 23andMe, a genetic testing and ancestry service, disclosed a data breach affecting 6.9 million users worldwide in December 2023. The breach exposed DNA ancestry data, personal profiles, and relationship information after attackers used stolen passwords from other breaches to access accounts. The company agreed to a $30 million settlement in 2024 to resolve class action lawsuits.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: A joint library network serving affluent Sydney local government areas—including Woollahra; Double Bay; Paddington; and Watsons Bay—suffered an external database intrusion that exposed the profile cards; emails; and borrowing records of thousands of local residents. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: One of Australia's largest charitable public and private healthcare operators; St Vincent’s Health Australia; suffered an uncontained corporate network intrusion. Threat actors successfully exfiltrated data folders from a centralized cloud storage system. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: St Vincent's Health Australia, a national Catholic healthcare provider operating public and private hospitals across multiple states, detected a cyber security incident on 19 December 2023. Forensic investigation found that approximately 4.3 gigabytes of system and network credential data was stolen, though no evidence of sensitive personal information theft was found. The attack was contained by 20 December 2023. The forensic investigation found that the stolen data was system and network credential data, with no evidence that sensitive personal information such as patient records or employee personal details was stolen. Whilst the investigation was ongoing, St Vincent's could not completely rule out the possibility that some personal information may have been accessed, though no evidence of such access was found.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Arts Centre Melbourne formally published a consumer data advisory disclosure indicating an isolated security incident on an internal database. The incident register reports: Independent threat monitors identified a recurrent data scraping leak displaying newly compiled backend profile records. The public-facing database contained user tracking identifiers; explicit account handles; unique device types; and system configuration configurations. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: High-level regulatory investigation initiated after a former Queensland Fire and Emergency Services (QFES) contractor retained unauthorized remote system tokens; enabling the continuing illicit extraction of sensitive internal Rural Fire Service operational datasets. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: The University of Wollongong (UOW) issued campus-wide notices confirming a severe perimeter network compromise. Advanced persistent threat (APT) actors penetrated primary student administration directories; targeting student files and academic verification histories. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: The University of Wollongong (UOW) confirmed a cyber incident on 7 December 2023 that likely resulted in unauthorised access to personal data of staff and students. The attack was quickly contained, with the university confirming that data including names, addresses, email addresses, and phone numbers was likely accessed. The university implemented new cloud security controls following the incident and warned users of potential phishing attacks.

records.summary: The incident register reports: Internal compliance reviews confirmed that the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) experienced four independent; internal system-error-driven data leaks since 2022; resulting in the accidental visibility of corporate registration entries. The incident register reports: A critical public sector supply chain incident targeting Aboriginal Family Support Services (AFSS); a contracted partner of the SA Department for Child Protection. Hacking groups extracted sensitive social work files; child protection case notes; and foster placements. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: A business email compromise (BEC) campaign targeted a prominent Brisbane medical center. Threat actors hijacked an administrative email account; granting unauthorized access to clinical appointment schedules; Medicare billing markers; and contact details for 5;000 patients. Incident type: Phishing; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: National corporate security and guarding services firm Certis Security confirmed an isolated business email compromise incident. Prompt detection by internal incident response teams prevented lateral movement or any downstream exposure of physical site security profiles. Incident type: Phishing; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Certis Security Australia suffered a breach of its email systems in November 2023 when personal information of some employees and partners was accessed by an unknown third party. The company stated that no customer data was affected. The breach was potentially linked to ransomware delivered via a phishing email, prompting the organisation to engage cybersecurity experts for investigation and remediation.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Major pathology collection aggregate Australian Clinical Labs (ACL) managed a severe secondary data leak stemming from an earlier infrastructure exploit. Exfiltrated files hosted on darknet platforms included specific patient medical test sheets; fertility tracking logs; and clinical markers. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: The National Disability Insurance Agency (NDIA) detected a significant privacy breach involving the systematic; unauthorized downloading and illicit third-party sharing of National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS) participant profile records by an inside actor. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Samsung disclosed that a cyber incident targeting its UK e-commerce storefront allowed unauthorized access to customer records. The breach resulted from an application vulnerability that exposed names; contact numbers; billing coordinates; and postal addresses. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Specialist Victorian pathology and biopsy laboratory TissuPath faced regulatory scrutiny following delayed notification routines to patients. A compromised third-party IT vendor repository exposed historical biopsy referrals and pathology order entries. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Major metropolitan Melbourne public hospital network Alfred Health confirmed a specialized database security breach. Unauthorized external threat actors targeted an administrative folder system; exposing specific patient clinical records and HIV tracking indices. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Alfred Health, Victoria's leading trauma hospital, discovered that a pharmacist had unauthorised access to approximately 7,000 patient medical records over a four-year period. The privacy breach, discovered in June 2023 and disclosed to patients in November, involved the pharmacist viewing records without clinical justification, including sensitive information of HIV patients. The pharmacist was dismissed following the investigation. While cybersecurity experts reviewing the incident found no evidence that patient information was downloaded or used beyond the unauthorised viewing, the breach still represented a serious violation of medical privacy and professional ethics.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Supply chain incident affecting SA Health via a third-party application; Digital Patient Pathways. A database parsing error and unauthenticated entry window resulted in the unauthorized erasure and potential brief exposure of patient orthopedic tracking lists. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Thousands of SA Health hospital patients were caught up in a supply chain cyber security breach targeting Personify Care; an outsourced digital patient intake and check-in vendor. Exfiltrated fields included clinical histories and check-in parameters. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Personify Care's Digital Patient Pathways platform experienced a data incident on 16 October 2023 affecting South Australian health patients. An unauthorised third party deleted a folder containing patient documents and contact information. Independent forensic analysis confirmed files were deleted but found no evidence of data being copied or downloaded. Independent forensic analysis confirmed that while files were deleted, no evidence was found indicating the data had been copied or downloaded by the unauthorised party. This suggests the incident was primarily data destruction rather than data theft.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: The AlphV ransomware group targeted the Victorian property management firm; infiltrating its local servers and exfiltrating sensitive tenant registries. The stolen file structures contained financial records; scanned driver's licenses; and private tenancy application dossiers. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: High. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Network Pacific Real Estate, a leading Victorian property company, was allegedly breached by the Ragnar Locker ransomware gang in October 2023. The attackers posted 30.6 gigabytes of data on 30 September 2023, claiming it contained personal information of employees and customers. Network Pacific did not publicly confirm the breach or publish any advisory on its website.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: South Australian public sector superannuation scheme Super SA disclosed a secondary data breach. The incident was traced to a compromised administrative email chain at an outsourced communication vendor; exposing member contribution updates. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Super SA, the South Australian government-owned superannuation provider, disclosed on 17 October 2023 that a former external call centre provider experienced a data breach affecting 14,011 members. The third-party provider, Contact 121, had been contracted in 2020 to handle inquiries from members affected by a separate 2019 breach but retained member data after the contract ended. Super SA became aware of the incident on 1 September 2023 but did not receive confirmation of the breach until 4 October.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: A successful business email compromise (BEC) campaign targeted a senior medical practitioner's Microsoft 365 profile at the Royal Women's Hospital in Melbourne. The threat actors monitored the inbox; gaining exposure to detailed care logs and identity data for 200 patients. Incident type: Phishing; source-rated severity: Critical. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: The Royal Women's Hospital in Melbourne apologised to 192 patients in October 2023 after their personal details were potentially stolen when cybercriminals gained unauthorised access to a staff member's private email account. The breach occurred because the employee had forwarded work emails containing patient information to their personal email account to review and coordinate patient appointments and care strategies. The hospital's official systems were not compromised.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Confirmed 6 Sep 2023. Landmark bookstore chain Dymocks issued a nationwide customer warning following a major darknet listing. A malicious entity successfully scraped its central customer loyalty database; leaking member emails; DOBs; and phone logs. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Dymocks, a major Australian bookstore chain, was informed of a data breach on 6 September 2023 after 1.24 million customer records appeared on hacking forums and the dark web. The breach was caused by unauthorised access to Dymocks' new loyalty programme provider's systems, where an attacker stole and used an access key to retrieve customer records. The stolen data, which had been circulating since at least June 2023, included names, dates of birth, email addresses, and postal addresses, but no financial information.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Landmark legal sector cyber attack. The ALPHV/BlackCat ransomware gang exfiltrated 2.5 million highly classified corporate files from elite law firm HWL Ebsworth. Stolen directories contained cabinet-level legal advice from 65 federal and state government departments. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Specialized downstream tracking link confirming that the Australian Federal Police (AFP) was heavily caught up in the HWL Ebsworth data disaster. Highly confidential operational litigation files and agent profiles were leaked to the dark web. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: The university disclosed a localized security incident involving a third-party application management service provider. The external breach allowed unauthorized access to sensitive applicant and recently enrolled student data platforms; forcing immediate portal lockouts. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: The University of Sydney disclosed a third-party data breach in August 2023 that affected a small proportion of international students and applicants. The breach involved a third-party service provider whose identity was not publicly disclosed. The university confirmed there was currently no evidence that personal information had been misused and that the issue was isolated to a single platform, with no impact on domestic students, employees, alumni, or donors. The university stated there was currently no evidence that any personal information had been misused, suggesting the breach was detected before significant harm could occur to affected individuals.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Telemarketing charity contractor Pareto Phone suffered a devastating data breach. Threat actors published an archive containing decades of historical donor lists on the dark web; impacting donors from multiple high-profile Australian charitable foundations. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Brisbane-based telemarketing firm Pareto Phone was attacked by the LockBit ransomware group in April 2023, resulting in the theft and dark web publication of 150GB of data affecting approximately 50,000 donors across 70 Australian charities. The breach was not disclosed to affected organisations until August 2023, and the stolen data included donor information dating back more than 15 years. The incident raised serious questions about data retention practices, with many charities unaware that Pareto had kept such historical donor records.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: The .au Domain Administration (auDA); the core regulatory governing body for Australian web domains; launched an intensive forensic investigation after a hacking group publicly claimed to have penetrated their administrative validation servers. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: In August 2023, the NoEscape ransomware gang claimed to have stolen 15GB of data from auDA (.au Domain Administration Limited), Australia's domain name administrator. After investigation, auDA determined its own systems were not breached—the data came from an Australian sole trader whose server was compromised on 10 August 2023. On 11 August 2023, the NoEscape ransomware group posted claims that they had breached auDA and stolen sensitive data. When auDA became aware of the claims on 18 August 2023, the organisation initially found no evidence of a breach of its systems.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Global automotive manufacturer Tesla confirmed that a significant historical data leak was executed intentionally by two rogue ex-employees who copied proprietary file structures to external personal drives; affecting Australian owners. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Tesla filed a notice of data breach with the Attorney General of Maine on 18 August 2023 after discovering that sensitive information belonging to more than 75,000 current and former employees was leaked by two former Tesla employees to German media outlet Handelsblatt. The investigation revealed that the two former employees misappropriated over 100 gigabytes of data containing 23,000 internal documents spanning from 2015 to 2022, violating Tesla's IT security and data protection policies. Tesla filed lawsuits and obtained court orders prohibiting the former employees from further use or dissemination of the data.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: A coordinated supply chain security breach targeted a shared corporate administrative service provider; resulting in the unauthorized extraction of non-public planning files and client interaction records linked to Judo Bank and Regional Express (Rex). Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: The federal Department of Veterans’ Affairs (DVA) managed an acute privacy failure after an unencrypted data reporting export accidentally exposed highly sensitive clinical medical treatment metrics of active and retired veterans to unauthorized channels. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: Wide-reaching supply chain cyber disaster tracking the exploitation of the Progress Software MOVEit Transfer zero-day vulnerability by the CL0P ransomware cartel. Dozens of major Australian enterprise networks utilizing the tool suffered file exfiltration. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Prominent medical research body QIMR Berghofer investigated a supply chain data breach affecting Australia’s largest historical skin cancer research trial database after an external cloud-hosted backup container was breached. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Global threat intelligence reports identified over 100;000 unique ChatGPT user credentials being actively traded on dark web illicit marketplaces. The data sets were compiled via widespread information-stealer malware infections running on end-user desktop and mobile devices. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: The Victorian State Government faced parliamentary scrutiny following a localized database breach within a regional youth and community engagement camping program platform; exposing participant emergency details and parent identity data. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: Massive identity fraud campaign leveraging credentials from historical breaches to manufacture fake myGov accounts linked to the Australian Taxation Office (ATO). Criminal networks successfully filed $557;000;000 in fraudulent tax refund claims. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: The National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS) formally detailed its enterprise exposure within the massive HWL Ebsworth law firm dark web leak; confirming that internal NDIS participant case dispute folders were caught up in the exfiltrated dataset. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Global electronic transaction giant PayPal implemented localized automated security freezes following a sharp acceleration in credential stuffing and high-grade smishing attacks that targeted consumer account authentication tokens across regional NSW. Incident type: Phishing; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: The federal Department of Home Affairs officially acknowledged an accidental privacy data leak wherein internal administrative web staff inadvertently published the proprietary personal and commercial data strings of 50 small business operators online. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: The South Australian division of the Liberal Party engaged state cyber police divisions after an advanced persistent threat group; theorized to be an Eastern European cyber gang; successfully breached an administrative web server hosting member indexes. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: State environmental management authority Parks Victoria suffered an extensive system outage following an unauthenticated web portal crash; triggering rigorous forensic evaluations into whether asset registration files were compromised. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Parks Victoria experienced a data breach on 4 July 2023 when launching its upgraded online booking system for the 2023/24 camping season. Due to extremely high demand, a technical flaw allowed a small number of users to see other people's booking details in the shopping cart section. The agency apologised and temporarily paused bookings while working with their supplier to fix the issues. A very small number of users were affected by the breach. Those impacted could see other people's booking details, including names, contact information, and reservation details. Parks Victoria's investigation found no evidence that sensitive information such as credit card details were compromised.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Coordinated investigation launched after a shared solar installer asset registration portal co-managed by LG Energy Solution Australia and Solar Service Guys was breached; exposing industrial customer residential solar battery logs. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: Historic national security breach wherein Russian-aligned state-sponsored threat actors successfully penetrated an external educational communication tool utilized by the Australian Defence Force; accessing non-classified personnel movement logs. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: EFTPOS and payment merchant solutions provider SmartPay launched an emergency incident response plan across Oceania operations to intercept an active data exfiltration pipeline targeting its merchant billing directory. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: SmartPay, Australasia's largest independently owned EFTPOS provider, suffered a ransomware attack in June 2023 that compromised customer data from its New Zealand systems. The attack was first detected on 10 June 2023, with confirmation of data theft announced on 16 June 2023. SmartPay engaged cybersecurity firm Cyber CX and worked with government authorities to respond to the incident.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Professional services giant PwC Australia confirmed its corporate environment was swept into the global MOVEit file transfer software exploit. Threat actors targeted institutional data containers holding retail logistical tracking lines. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Technical reviews clarified that a security scare at the Port Arthur historic library database was caused by human administrative error; where a developer inadvertently set internal employee profile charts to live public view" during server moves." Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: The ACT Government officially disclosed a multi-agency system breach stemming directly from the widespread exploitation of the Fortra GoAnywhere file transfer service zero-day vulnerability by the CL0P syndicates. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: The ACT Government detected a security breach in its Barracuda email gateway system in June 2023, affecting email screening for various government directorates including Access Canberra, health, and education. Barracuda Networks notified customers on 24 May 2023 of a vulnerability, and the ACT Cyber Security Centre immediately completed a rebuild of the impacted system. Investigation by Mandiant identified infrastructure and malware code overlaps indicating "a high degree of confidence that this is a China-nexus espionage operation." Following completion of phase one of the investigation, there was no definitive evidence of information being removed or misused.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Ambulance Victoria's critical business continuity systems suffered exposure after a cyber attack compromised its external cloud-based rostering vendor. The breach exposed operational shift schedules; partial medical practitioner details; and regional emergency services rostering frameworks. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Ambulance Victoria was made aware on 11 May 2023 that documents containing confidential drug and alcohol testing results of approximately 600 job applicants were accessible to all Ambulance Victoria employees on the organisation's intranet. The documents, which related to testing conducted between May 2017 and October 2018, included first names, last names, test dates, results, and where applicable, the class of drug detected. The breach occurred due to an error that made the documents accessible internally, though they were not available outside the organisation. An investigation showed the documents had been accessed only a handful of times in the past six months. The documents were not directly accessible to anyone outside the organisation, and there was no evidence of them being shared outside Ambulance Victoria.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: An independent security researcher discovered an open; completely unsecured cloud database belonging to the free VPN service. The exposed cluster contained hundreds of millions of logs detailing user email addresses; real-world IP addresses; localized geolocation tracking markers; and internet connection logs. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: High.

The incident register reports: Post-incident evaluation into Fire Rescue Victoria’s comprehensive cyber security recovery response; highlighting intense union and internal pushback regarding delayed communication chains following server exfiltration. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Severe public sector data handling incident wherein NT Government health staff accidentally transmitted thousands of fully identifiable clinical patient records and treatment profiles to an unverified software vendor located overseas. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: Automotive giant Toyota Motor Corporation disclosed a catastrophic decade-long cloud database misconfiguration. Due to a cloud access control error; consumer vehicle telemetry strings and registration markers sat exposed online from 2013 to 2023. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: Toyota confirmed in May 2023 that a comparatively small number of Australian customers' records were impacted after a misconfigured cloud database made vehicle and customer data publicly accessible. The global breach primarily affected 2.15 million users in Japan, with vehicle location information exposed for nearly 10 years between November 2013 and April 2023. Australian customers affected had vehicle information and some personal data such as names and contact information exposed, but no personal financial details were compromised.
records.sourceLabel: Supplied incident register (unverified); Australian Data Breach Archive

records.summary: The incident register reports: Landmark Australian cyber disaster. Russian-based threat actors (REvil/BlogXX) exfiltrated 520GB of highly sensitive medical insurance claims databases. 9.7M customers affected. Following non-payment of ransom; data including terminations and addiction treatments was leaked. Threat actor Aleksandr Ermakov was formally sanctioned globally; OAIC issued a $21.5M fine. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: The Money Message ransomware group successfully exfiltrated proprietary firmware frameworks from MSI's corporate network. The leaked archives contained private cryptographic signing keys; Intel Boot Guard certificates; and BIOS source code frameworks impacting multiple computing product lines. Incident type: Ransomware; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: Localized commercial supply chain database leakage identified during routine automated scanning; exposing transport data structures and cross-docking performance logs compiled for internal industry performance metrics. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Non-profit human rights advocacy body Amnesty International Australia finalized remediation reports following a historical December server breach; implementing end-to-end encryption across donor and volunteer registry vaults. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Historic telecommunications cyber catastrophe. An unauthenticated API gateway configuration allowed automated scraping of Optus customer records. 9.8M accounts breached; including names; DOBs; and addresses. 2.1M users had active driver's licence and passport numbers stolen; triggering a massive national identity re-issuing campaign and class-action litigation. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Critical.

The incident register reports: Elite class-action lawsuits initiated by corporate institutional shareholders against Afterpay's parent operating entity; Block Inc.; alleging failure to provide timely regulatory stock market disclosures regarding historical internal data breach windows. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium.

The incident register reports: Intellectual property management conglomerate IPH Limited disclosed an enterprise data security breach; tracking the source vector to a network perimeter compromise inside member patent attorney firm Spruson & Ferguson. Incident type: Data Breach; source-rated severity: Medium. The Australian Data Breach Archive reports: IPH Limited, the parent company of intellectual property law firms Spruson & Ferguson and Griffith Hack, detected unauthorised access to a portion of its IT environment on 13 March 2023. A forensic investigation revealed that a limited set of data originating from Spruson & Ferguson (Australia) was downloaded by an unauthorised third party. The downloaded data contained information relating to certain clients of that practice, as well as some historical financial and corporate information. IPH estimated $2-2.5 million in non-underlying costs related to the incident response. A forensic probe into the data breach revealed that whilst multiple systems were accessed, only a limited set of data was actually downloaded.
